sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十九】 起昭陽單瘀七月，盡旃蒙大荒落十月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 39] From the seventh month of Zhaoyang Danju through the tenth month of Zhanmeng Dahuangluo; a little more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 39] From the seventh month of Zhaoyang Danju through the tenth month of Zhanmeng Dahuangluo—a span of slightly more than two years.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝上之下廣德元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong the Sagely, Cultured, Filial, and Martial — first part, lower section — first year of Guangde (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong the Sagely, Cultured, Filial, and Martial (lower fascicle), first year of Guangde (

sentences.zh: 癸卯，公元七六三年）

translations.literal: Guimao, corresponding to 763 CE).
translations.idiomatic: guimao, 763 CE).

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬寅，群臣上尊號曰寶應元聖文武孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, the officials submitted a honorific title: Emperor Baoying Yuansheng Wenwu Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, the courtiers presented the honorific title Baoying Yuansheng Wenwu Xiao Emperor.

sentences.zh: 壬子，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On renzi, he proclaimed a general amnesty for the empire and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he pardoned the empire and declared a new reign era.

sentences.zh: 諸將討史朝義者進官階、加爵邑有差。

translations.literal: The generals who had campaigned against Shi Chaoyi were promoted in rank and granted fiefs in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The generals who had suppressed Shi Chaoyi were advanced in office and ennobled with estates, each according to merit.

sentences.zh: 冊回紇可汗為頡咄登蜜施合俱錄英義建功毘伽可汗，可敦為娑墨光親麗華毘伽可敦；

translations.literal: The Uyghur qaghan was enfeoffed as Qiedudeng Mishigejulü Yingyi Jiangong Pijia Qaghan; his consort as Suomoguangqin Lihua Pijia Kedun;
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur qaghan was invested as Qiedudeng Mishigejulü Yingyi Jiangong Pijia Qaghan, and his consort as Suomoguangqin Lihua Pijia Kedun;

sentences.zh: 左、右殺以下，皆加封賞。

translations.literal: From the Left and Right Shas downward, all received additional titles and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: All ranks from the Left and Right Shas down received further honors and gifts.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，楊綰上貢舉條目：秀才問經義二十條，對策五道；

translations.literal: On wuchen, Yang Wan submitted examination regulations: for xiucai, twenty questions on the meaning of the classics and five policy essays;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Yang Wan proposed civil-service examination rules: candidates for xiucai would answer twenty questions on classical meaning and five policy essays;

sentences.zh: 國子監舉人，令博士薦於祭酒，祭酒試通者升之於省，如鄉貢法。

translations.literal: for Guozijian candidates, erudites were to recommend them to the libationer; those who passed the libationer's examination would be advanced to the provincial board, as under the local-recommendation method.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy students would be nominated by erudites to the libationer, who would test them and send those who passed on to the provincial examinations, following the same procedure as the local-recommendation system.

sentences.zh: 明法，委刑部考試。

translations.literal: For mingfa, examination was entrusted to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Legal specialists would be examined by the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 或以為明經、進士，行之已久，不可遽改。

translations.literal: Some held that the mingjing and jinshi examinations had long been in use and could not be abruptly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that the mingjing and jinshi tracks had been established for so long that they ought not be changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行。

translations.literal: The proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The reforms were not enacted.

sentences.zh: 識者是之。

translations.literal: Those of insight approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment nevertheless approved of Yang Wan's plan.

sentences.zh: 以僕固瑒為朔方行營節度使。

translations.literal: Pugu Chang was appointed military commissioner of the Shuofang field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Chang was made military commissioner of the Shuofang field command.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃入大震關，陷蘭、廓、河、鄯、洮、岷、秦、成、渭等州，盡取河西、隴右之地。

translations.literal: The Tibetans entered Dazhen Pass and captured Lan, Kuo, He, Shan, Tao, Min, Qin, Cheng, Wei, and other prefectures, taking all the territory of Hexi and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans broke through Dazhen Pass and overran Lan, Kuo, He, Shan, Tao, Min, Qin, Cheng, Wei, and other prefectures, seizing the whole of the Hexi and Longyou regions.

sentences.zh: 唐自武德以來，開拓邊境，地連西域，皆置都督、府、州、縣。

translations.literal: Since the Wude era the Tang had expanded the frontier until their lands joined the Western Regions, establishing protectorates, prefectures, districts, and counties throughout.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wude reign onward the Tang had pushed the frontier westward until it met the Western Regions, dotting the borderlands with protectorates, prefectures, districts, and counties.

sentences.zh: 開元中，置朔方、隴右、河西、安西、北庭諸節度使以統之，歲發山東丁壯為戍卒，繒帛為軍資，開屯田，供糗糧，設監牧，畜馬牛，軍城戍邏，萬里相望。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period military commissioners of Shuofang, Longyou, Hexi, Anxi, and Beiting were established to command them; each year men from east of the mountains were levied as garrison troops, silk as military funds; garrison farms were opened to supply grain; pasture offices were set up to raise horses and cattle; fortresses and posts lined the border for ten thousand li, visible one to another.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan, commissioners for Shuofang, Longyou, Hexi, Anxi, and Beiting were appointed to govern the frontier. Each year able-bodied men from east of the mountains were drafted as garrison soldiers, silk allotted for military expenses, farms opened to feed the troops, and pasture offices established to breed horses and cattle. Fortresses and watchposts stretched along the border for thousands of li, each within sight of the next.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，邊兵精銳者皆征發入援，謂之行營，所留兵單弱，胡虜稍蠶食之；

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, the crack border troops were all mobilized for relief — called the field armies — and those left behind were few and weak; the barbarians gradually nibbled away at them;
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in revolt, the best border troops were summoned east as field armies, leaving only thin garrisons behind; steppe peoples slowly gnawed away at the frontier;

sentences.zh: 數年間，西北數十州相繼淪沒，自鳳翔以西，邠州以北，皆為左衽矣。

translations.literal: Within a few years dozens of northwestern prefectures fell in succession; from Fengxiang westward and Binzhou northward, all wore the barbarian lapel.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years dozens of northwestern prefectures fell one after another; from Fengxiang west and Binzhou north, the land passed entirely to foreign rule.

sentences.zh: 初，僕固懷恩受詔與回紇可汗相見於太原；

translations.literal: Earlier, Pugu Huai'en had received orders to meet the Uyghur qaghan at Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Pugu Huai'en had been ordered to meet the Uyghur qaghan at Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 河東節度使辛雲京以可汗乃懷恩婿，恐其合謀襲軍府，閉城自守，亦不犒師。

translations.literal: the Hedong military commissioner Xin Yunjing, because the qaghan was Huai'en's son-in-law, feared they would conspire to attack his headquarters, shut the city and held it alone, and would not reward the troops either.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong commissioner Xin Yunjing, knowing the qaghan was Huai'en's son-in-law, feared a joint strike on his headquarters, barred the gates, and refused even to entertain the army.

sentences.zh: 及史朝義既平，詔懷恩送可汗出塞，往來過太原，雲京亦閉城不與相聞。

translations.literal: When Shi Chaoyi had been pacified, Huai'en was ordered to escort the qaghan beyond the border; passing Taiyuan again in both directions, Yunjing again shut the city and would not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Chaoyi was crushed, Huai'en was commanded to escort the qaghan home; traveling through Taiyuan again in both directions, Yunjing once more shut the gates and refused all contact.

sentences.zh: 懷恩怒，具表其狀，不報。

translations.literal: Huai'en was enraged and submitted a full memorial on the matter; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was furious and memorialized the court in full detail, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 懷恩將朔方兵數萬屯汾州，使其子御史大夫瑒將萬人屯榆次，裨將李光逸等屯祈縣，李懷光等屯晉州，張維岳等屯沁州。

translations.literal: Huai'en led several tens of thousands of Shuofang troops stationed at Fenzhou; his son the censor-in-chief Chang led ten thousand at Yuci; lieutenants Li Guangyi and others at Qixian; Li Huaiguang and others at Jinzhou; Zhang Weiyue and others at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en camped tens of thousands of Shuofang troops at Fenzhou, sent his son Chang, the chief censor, with ten thousand men to Yuci, and posted Li Guangyi and other lieutenants at Qixian, Li Huaiguang at Jinzhou, and Zhang Weiyue at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷光，本勃海靺鞨也，姓茹，為朔方將，以功賜姓。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was originally a Mohe of Bohai, surname Ru; he was a Shuofang general and received the imperial surname for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was a Bohai Mohe by origin, family name Ru; he served as a Shuofang general and was granted the imperial surname Li for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 中使駱奉仙至太原，雲京厚結之，為言懷恩與回紇連謀，反狀已露。

translations.literal: The palace envoy Luo Fengxian arrived at Taiyuan; Yunjing cultivated him lavishly and told him that Huai'en was in league with the Uyghurs and that signs of rebellion had already appeared.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace envoy Luo Fengxian reached Taiyuan, Yunjing won him over with lavish favors and told him Huai'en was plotting with the Uyghurs and that treason was already plain.

sentences.zh: 奉仙還，過懷恩，懷恩與飲於母前，母數讓奉仙曰：「汝與吾兒約為兄弟，今又親雲京，何兩面也！」

translations.literal: Fengxian returned, passed by Huai'en, and Huai'en drank with him before his mother; the mother repeatedly reproached Fengxian, saying, "You and my son pledged brotherhood — now you side with Yunjing. How two-faced!"
translations.idiomatic: On his return Fengxian stopped at Huai'en's camp, where Huai'en entertained him in his mother's presence. The old lady rebuked Fengxian repeatedly: "You and my son swore brotherhood — yet now you cozy up to Yunjing. What double-dealing is this!"

sentences.zh: 酒酣，懷恩起舞，奉仙贈以纏頭彩。

translations.literal: When the wine was warm, Huai'en danced; Fengxian gave him a turban-ribbon of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed, Huai'en rose to dance, and Fengxian presented him with a silk head-wrap.

sentences.zh: 懷恩欲酬之，曰：「來日端午，當更樂飲一日。」

translations.literal: Huai'en wished to return the gift and said, "Tomorrow is the Dragon Boat Festival — we should feast again for a day."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en meant to repay the gift and said, "Tomorrow is the Dragon Boat Festival — let us drink together once more."

sentences.zh: 奉仙固請行，懷恩匿其馬，奉仙謂左右曰：「朝來責我，又匿我馬，將殺我也。」

translations.literal: Fengxian pressed to leave; Huai'en hid his horse. Fengxian said to his attendants, "This morning they scolded me, and now they hide my horse — they mean to kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian insisted on departing, but Huai'en concealed his horse. Fengxian told his men, "They berated me this morning and now they hide my horse — they intend to kill me."

sentences.zh: 夜，逾垣而走；

translations.literal: By night he climbed the wall and fled;
translations.idiomatic: That night he scaled the wall and fled;

sentences.zh: 懷恩驚，遽以其馬追還之。

translations.literal: Huai'en was alarmed and hastily sent his horse after him to bring him back.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was startled and at once sent his own horse after him to fetch him back.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸未，奉仙至長安，奏懷恩謀反；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guiwei, Fengxian reached Chang'an and reported that Huai'en was plotting rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guiwei, Fengxian reached Chang'an and accused Huai'en of treason;

sentences.zh: 懷恩亦具奏其狀，請誅雲京、奉仙；

translations.literal: Huai'en also submitted a full account and asked that Yunjing and Fengxian be executed;
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en likewise memorialized in full and demanded the execution of Yunjing and Fengxian;

sentences.zh: 上兩無所問，優詔和解之。

translations.literal: the emperor questioned neither side and issued a gracious edict to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor took no action against either party and issued a gracious edict urging reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 懷恩自以兵興以來，所在力戰，一門死王事者四十六人，女嫁絕域，說諭回紇，再收兩京，平定河南、北，功無與比，而為人構陷，憤怨殊深，上書自訟，以為：「臣昨奉詔送可汗歸國，傾竭家資，俾之上道。

translations.literal: Huai'en considered that since the outbreak of war he had fought fiercely everywhere; forty-six of his clan had died in the emperor's service; his daughters had married into distant lands; he had persuaded the Uyghurs, recovered both capitals, and pacified Henan and Hebei — achievements unmatched — yet he was framed by others and his resentment ran very deep. He submitted a memorial in his own defense, stating: "Your servant recently received orders to escort the qaghan home and exhausted the family fortune to send him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en felt that since the rebellion began he had fought everywhere with all his strength: forty-six of his household had died for the throne, his daughters had been married into distant lands, he had won over the Uyghurs, retaken both capitals, and pacified Henan and Hebei — feats without parallel — yet others had framed him, and his anger ran deep. He memorialized in his own defense: "When I was lately ordered to escort the qaghan home, I drained my family's wealth to speed him on his way.

sentences.zh: 行至山北，雲京、奉仙閉城不出祗迎，仍令潛行竊盜。

translations.literal: When we reached north of the mountains, Yunjing and Fengxian shut their cities and would not come out to receive us, and even sent men to steal by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: North of the mountains, Yunjing and Fengxian barred their gates and refused a proper welcome, and even sent thieves to plunder us in secret.

sentences.zh: 回紇怨怒，亟欲縱兵，臣力為彌縫，方得出塞。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs were furious and eager to unleash their troops; your servant strove to mediate before they could leave the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were enraged and eager to attack; only by my strenuous mediation did they consent to leave the frontier.

sentences.zh: 雲京、奉仙恐臣先有奏論，遂復妄稱設備，與李抱玉共相組織。

translations.literal: Yunjing and Fengxian, fearing that your servant had already memorialized, falsely claimed defensive preparations and conspired with Li Baoyu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing I had already reported them, Yunjing and Fengxian invented tales of defensive preparations and conspired with Li Baoyu against me.

sentences.zh: 臣靜而思之，其罪有六：昔同羅叛亂，臣為先帝掃清河曲，一也；

translations.literal: Your servant reflects calmly: my crimes number six. Formerly when the Tongluo rebelled, your servant swept the Qinghe bend for the late emperor — the first;
translations.idiomatic: On reflection, my offenses are six in number. When the Tongluo rebelled, I cleared the Qinghe bend for the late emperor — first;

sentences.zh: 臣男玢為同羅所虜，得間亡歸，臣斬之以令眾士，二也；

translations.literal: your servant's son Bin was captured by the Tongluo, escaped when he could, and your servant executed him to command the troops — the second;
translations.idiomatic: my son Bin was captured by the Tongluo and escaped when he could; I executed him to stiffen the troops' resolve — second;

sentences.zh: 臣有二女，遠嫁外夷，為國和親，蕩平寇敵，三也；

translations.literal: your servant had two daughters married far among barbarians for the state's marriage alliances and to sweep away the enemy — the third;
translations.idiomatic: I gave two daughters in marriage to distant peoples for the state's alliances and to help crush the rebels — third;

sentences.zh: 臣與男瑒不顧死亡，為國效命，四也；

translations.literal: your servant and his son Chang disregarded death and served the state — the fourth;
translations.idiomatic: my son Chang and I have faced death without flinching in the state's service — fourth;

sentences.zh: 河北新附，節度使皆握強兵，臣撫綏以安反側，五也；

translations.literal: Hebei had newly submitted and the military commissioners all held strong armies; your servant pacified them to settle those who might turn — the fifth;
translations.idiomatic: when Hebei had just submitted and every commissioner held a strong army, I soothed them to quiet restless hearts — fifth;

sentences.zh: 臣說諭回紇，使赴急難，天下既平，送之歸國，六也。

translations.literal: your servant persuaded the Uyghurs to come to urgent aid; when the realm was pacified, he sent them home — the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: I persuaded the Uyghurs to answer the empire's call, and when peace returned, escorted them home — sixth.

sentences.zh: 臣既負六罪，誠合萬誅，惟當吞恨九泉，銜冤千古，復何訴哉！

translations.literal: Having these six crimes, your servant truly deserves ten thousand executions; he can only swallow his bitterness in the nine springs and bear his wrong through the ages — to whom can he appeal!
translations.idiomatic: With six such crimes to my name, I deserve death a thousand times over; I can only choke on my grief in the grave and carry this injustice forever — to whom may I appeal?

sentences.zh: 臣受恩至重，夙夜思奉天顏，但以來瑱受誅，朝廷不示其罪，諸道節度，誰不疑懼！

translations.literal: Your servant has received grace beyond measure and night and day longs to behold the heavenly countenance; but since Lai Tian was executed and the court did not show his crime, which military commissioner on every circuit does not doubt and fear!
translations.idiomatic: I owe Your Majesty boundless grace and long day and night to see your face; yet when Lai Tian was put to death without the court stating his crime, which commissioner in the land did not grow fearful?

sentences.zh: 近聞詔追數人，盡皆不至，實畏中官讒口，虛受陛下誅夷；

translations.literal: Recently it was heard that several men were summoned by edict and none came — they truly fear the eunuchs' slander and expect to suffer Your Majesty's execution in vain;
translations.idiomatic: Lately several men were summoned by imperial edict and none obeyed — they truly dread the eunuchs' slanders and expect to die on Your Majesty's order without cause;

sentences.zh: 豈惟群臣不忠，正為回邪在側。

translations.literal: it is not only that the ministers are disloyal — it is because perverse men stand at your side.
translations.idiomatic: it is not that your ministers lack loyalty, but that wicked counselors stand at your side.

sentences.zh: 且臣前後所奏駱奉仙，詞情非不摭實，陛下竟無處置，寵任彌深；

translations.literal: Moreover, your servant's successive memorials against Luo Fengxian were by no means without factual basis, yet Your Majesty took no action and his favor grew ever deeper;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my repeated memorials against Luo Fengxian were grounded in fact, yet Your Majesty took no action and his favor only deepened;

sentences.zh: 皆由同類比周，蒙蔽聖聽。

translations.literal: all because their kind band together and blind the sage's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: all because their kind band together and blind Your Majesty to the truth.

sentences.zh: 竊聞四方遣人奏事，陛下皆雲與驃騎議之，曾不委宰相可否，或稽留數月不還，遠近益加疑阻。

translations.literal: It is privately heard that when men from the four quarters are sent to memorialize, Your Majesty always says you will discuss it with the Biaoji — never entrusting approval or rejection to the chancellors, or detaining them for months without return — so that near and far grow ever more suspicious and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that when envoys from the provinces come to report, Your Majesty always says you will consult the Biaoji, never leaving matters to the chancellors, and sometimes detains them for months — so that suspicion deepens everywhere.

sentences.zh: 如臣朔方將士，功效最高，為先帝中興主人，乃陛下蒙塵故吏，曾不別加優獎，反信讒嫉之詞。

translations.literal: Such men as your servant's Shuofang soldiers, whose achievements are highest, who were the late emperor's agents of restoration and Your Majesty's old officers from the days of dust on the throne — they have received no special reward but instead suffer slander and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: My Shuofang troops, whose merit stands highest, who restored the late emperor and served Your Majesty in your days of exile — have received no special favor, while slander is believed against them.

sentences.zh: 子儀先已被猜，臣今又遭詆毀，弓藏鳥盡，信匪虛言。

translations.literal: Ziyi was already suspected before; your servant now suffers slander in turn — when the bow is stored the birds are spent: the saying is no empty phrase.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was already suspected; now I too am slandered — when the bow is laid away the birds are done for: the proverb is no empty saying.

sentences.zh: 陛下信其矯誣，何殊指鹿為馬！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty believes their fabrications, how is it different from calling a deer a horse!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty believes their fabrications, what difference is there from calling a deer a horse!

sentences.zh: 倘不納愚懇，且貴因循，臣實不敢保家，陛下豈能安國！

translations.literal: If you do not accept this foolish plea and instead prize delay, your servant truly dares not secure his household — how can Your Majesty secure the state!
translations.idiomatic: If you will not heed this humble plea and prize delay instead, I dare not hope to keep my household safe — how then can Your Majesty keep the realm secure!

sentences.zh: 忠言利行，惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: Loyal words benefit action — may Your Majesty consider them.
translations.idiomatic: Honest counsel serves the realm well — I beg Your Majesty to weigh it.

sentences.zh: 臣欲公然入朝，恐將士留沮。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to enter court openly but fears the troops will detain and obstruct him.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to come to court openly, but fear my soldiers will hold me back.

sentences.zh: 今托巡晉、絳，於彼遷延，乞陛下特遣一介至絳州問臣，臣即與之同發。」

translations.literal: Now, under the pretext of patrolling Jin and Jiang, he delays there; he begs Your Majesty specially to send a single envoy to Jiangzhou to inquire of your servant, and your servant will set out with him at once."
translations.idiomatic: I now plead a tour of Jin and Jiang and linger there; I beg Your Majesty to send a single envoy to Jiangzhou to summon me, and I will set out with him at once."

sentences.zh: 九月，壬戌，上遣裴遵慶詣懷恩諭旨，且察其去就。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renxu, the emperor sent Pei Zunqing to Huai'en to convey the imperial will and observe his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu, the emperor sent Pei Zunqing to Huai'en to deliver the imperial message and gauge his intentions.

sentences.zh: 懷恩見遵慶，抱其足號泣拆冤。

translations.literal: Huai'en met Zunqing, embraced his feet, and wept aloud proclaiming his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en met Zunqing, clasped his feet, and wept aloud as he pleaded his innocence.

sentences.zh: 遵慶為言聖恩優厚，諷令入朝，懷恩許諾。

translations.literal: Zunqing spoke of the emperor's gracious favor and hinted that he should enter court; Huai'en promised.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing spoke of the emperor's gracious favor and urged him to come to court; Huai'en agreed.

sentences.zh: 副將范志誠以為不可，曰：「公信其甘言，入則為來瑱，不復還矣！」

translations.literal: The deputy general Fan Zhicheng held it impossible and said, "Your Lordship believes their sweet words — if you enter court you will be another Lai Tian and never return!"
translations.idiomatic: Deputy general Fan Zhicheng objected: "Your Lordship trusts their honeyed words — enter court and you will share Lai Tian's fate and never return!"

sentences.zh: 明日，懷恩見遵慶，以懼死為辭，請令一子入朝，志誠又以為不可，遵慶乃還。

translations.literal: The next day Huai'en met Zunqing and, pleading fear of death, asked to send one son to court instead; Zhicheng again held it impossible, and Zunqing returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Huai'en met Zunqing, pleaded fear of death, and asked to send a son to court in his stead; Zhicheng again objected, and Zunqing returned.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫王翊使回紇還，懷恩先與可汗往來，恐翊洩其事，遂留之。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Wang Yi returned from his mission to the Uyghurs; Huai'en had earlier had dealings with the qaghan and, fearing Yi would leak the matter, detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief censor Wang Yi returned from his mission to the Uyghurs; Huai'en, who had earlier dealt with the qaghan, feared Yi would reveal too much and detained him.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃之初入寇也，邊將告急，程元振皆不以聞。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans first invaded, border generals reported emergencies, but Cheng Yuanzhen relayed none of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans first raided the frontier, border commanders sent urgent reports, but Cheng Yuanzhen suppressed them all.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，吐蕃寇涇州，刺史高暉以城降之，遂為之鄉導，引吐蕃深入；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Tibetans raided Jingzhou; the prefect Gao Hui surrendered the city and then served as their guide, leading the Tibetans deep inland;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Tibetans attacked Jingzhou; prefect Gao Hui surrendered the city and then guided them inland;

sentences.zh: 過邠州，上始聞之。

translations.literal: when they passed Binzhou the emperor first heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: only when they passed Binzhou did the emperor first learn of the invasion.

sentences.zh: 辛未，寇奉天、武功，京師震駭。

translations.literal: On xinwei they raided Fengtian and Wugong; the capital was shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei they struck Fengtian and Wugong, and the capital was convulsed with fear.

sentences.zh: 詔以雍王適為關內元帥，郭子儀為副元帥，出鎮咸陽以御之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Prince Yong Shi as commander-in-chief of Guannei and Guo Ziyi as deputy commander; they went out to garrison Xianyang to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Prince Yong Shi commander-in-chief of Guannei and Guo Ziyi his deputy, and sent them to hold Xianyang against the invaders.

sentences.zh: 子儀閒廢日久，部曲離散，至是召募，得二十騎而行，至咸陽，吐蕃帥吐谷渾、党項、氐、羌二十餘萬眾，瀰漫數十里，已自司竹園渡渭，循山而東。

translations.literal: Ziyi had long been idle and dismissed; his followers had scattered; now he recruited and mustered only twenty horsemen to set out. Reaching Xianyang, he found more than two hundred thousand Tibetans, Tuyuhun, Tangut, Di, and Qiang stretching for dozens of li; they had already crossed the Wei at Sizhu Garden and were moving east along the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi had long been sidelined and his followers scattered; he now scraped together only twenty horsemen. At Xianyang he faced more than two hundred thousand Tibetans, Tuyuhun, Tangut, Di, and Qiang spread across dozens of li — they had already crossed the Wei at Sizhu Garden and were marching east along the foothills.

sentences.zh: 子儀使判官中書舍人王延昌入奏，請益兵，程元振遏之，竟不召見。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent his aide, Secretariat drafter Wang Yanchang, to memorialize and request reinforcements; Cheng Yuanzhen blocked it, and he was never received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent his aide, Secretariat drafter Wang Yanchang, to request reinforcements; Cheng Yuanzhen blocked the message, and the emperor never granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，渭北行營兵馬使呂月將將精卒二千，破吐蕃於盩厔之西。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Lü Yuejiang, army horse commissioner of the Weibei field headquarters, with two thousand picked troops defeated the Tibetans west of Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Lü Yuejiang of the Weibei field command, with two thousand elite troops, routed the Tibetans west of Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，吐蕃寇盩厔，月將復與力戰，兵盡，為虜所擒。

translations.literal: On yihai the Tibetans raided Zhouzhi; Yuejiang fought again with all his strength; his troops were exhausted and he was captured by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Tibetans attacked Zhouzhi; Yuejiang fought again until his men were spent and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 上方治兵，而吐蕃已度便橋，倉猝不知所為。

translations.literal: The emperor was just drilling troops when the Tibetans had already crossed Bian Bridge; in the sudden crisis he knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still mustering troops when the Tibetans had already crossed Bian Bridge; caught off guard, he did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 丙子，出幸陝州，官吏藏竄，六軍逃散。

translations.literal: On bingzi he fled in favor to Shazhou; officials hid and fled; the Six Armies scattered.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi he fled to Shazhou; officials went into hiding and the Six Armies broke apart.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀聞之，遽自咸陽歸長安，比至，車駕已去。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi heard of it and hastened from Xianyang back to Chang'an; by the time he arrived, the imperial carriage had already departed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi heard the news and rushed from Xianyang to Chang'an, but by the time he arrived the emperor had already fled.

sentences.zh: 上才出苑門，渡滻水，射生將王獻忠擁四百騎叛還長安，脅豐王珙等十王西迎吐蕃。

translations.literal: The emperor had just left the park gate and crossed the Ba River when the hunting general Wang Xianzhong, with four hundred horsemen, mutinied and returned to Chang'an, coercing Prince Feng Gong and nine other princes to go west and welcome the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had barely left the park gate and crossed the Ba River when hunting general Wang Xianzhong, with four hundred horsemen, mutinied, returned to Chang'an, and forced Prince Feng Gong and nine other princes to ride west and welcome the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 遇子儀於開遠門內，子儀叱之，獻忠下馬，謂子儀曰：「今主上東遷，社稷無主，令公身為元帥，廢立在一言耳。」

translations.literal: They met Ziyi inside the Kaiyuan Gate; Ziyi rebuked him; Xianzhong dismounted and said to Ziyi, "Now the sovereign has moved east and the altars of state are without a master; Your Lordship is the commander — deposition and enthronement hang on a single word."
translations.idiomatic: They met Guo Ziyi inside the Kaiyuan Gate. Guo Ziyi rebuked him; Xianzhong dismounted and said, "The sovereign has fled east and the throne stands empty; you are the commander — deposition and enthronement rest on a single word from you."

sentences.zh: 子儀未應。

translations.literal: Ziyi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi did not answer.

sentences.zh: 珙越次言曰：「公何不言！」

translations.literal: Gong spoke out of turn: "Why does Your Lordship not speak!"
translations.idiomatic: Gong broke in: "Why do you not speak!"

sentences.zh: 子儀責讓之，以兵援送行在。

translations.literal: Ziyi rebuked and reproached him and sent troops to escort the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi rebuked him sharply and sent troops to escort the imperial party.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，車駕至華州，官吏奔散，無復供擬，扈從將士不免凍餒。

translations.literal: On dingchou the imperial carriage reached Huazhou; officials had fled and scattered; there were no supplies; the escorting soldiers could not escape cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the imperial party reached Huazhou; officials had fled and no provisions could be found; the escorting troops went hungry and cold.

sentences.zh: 會觀軍容使魚朝恩將神策軍自陝來迎，上乃幸朝恩營。

translations.literal: It happened that the army-inspecting commissioner Yu Chao'en led the Shence Army from Shan to welcome him, and the emperor then visited Chao'en's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Army-inspecting commissioner Yu Chao'en arrived from Shan with the Shence Army to welcome him, and the emperor took refuge in Chao'en's camp.

sentences.zh: 豐王珙見上於潼關，上不之責，退至幕中，有不遜語；

translations.literal: Prince Feng Gong met the emperor at Tong Pass; the emperor did not reproach him; retiring to his tent, he spoke insolently;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Feng Gong met the emperor at Tong Pass; the emperor did not rebuke him, but in his tent afterward the prince spoke insolently;

sentences.zh: 群臣奏請誅之，乃賜死。

translations.literal: the ministers memorialized requesting his execution, and he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: the ministers memorialized for his execution, and he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，吐蕃入長安，高暉與吐蕃大將馬重英等立故邠王守禮之孫廣武王承宏為帝，改元，置百官，以前翰林學士於可封等為相。

translations.literal: On wuyin the Tibetans entered Chang'an; Gao Hui and the Tibetan general Ma Chongying and others enthroned Guangwu Prince Chenghong, grandson of the former Prince of Bin Shouli, as emperor, changed the reign title, established the hundred offices, and made the former Hanlin academician Yu Kefeng and others chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Tibetans occupied Chang'an; Gao Hui and the Tibetan general Ma Chongying installed Guangwu Prince Chenghong, grandson of the former Prince of Bin Shouli, as emperor, proclaimed a new reign era, set up a full bureaucracy, and appointed the former Hanlin academician Yu Kefeng and others as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃剽掠府庫市裡，焚閭捨，長安中蕭然一空。

translations.literal: The Tibetans plundered the treasuries and market wards, burned houses, and Chang'an was desolate and empty.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans looted the treasuries and markets, burned neighborhoods, and Chang'an was left utterly desolate.

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿病臥家，遣人輿入，迫脅之，晉卿閉口不言，虜不敢殺。

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing lay ill at home; they sent men to carry him in a litter and coerced him; Jinqing kept his mouth closed and would not speak; the barbarians did not dare kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing lay ill at home; they had him carried in on a litter and tried to coerce him, but he would not speak, and the invaders did not dare kill him.

sentences.zh: 於是六軍散者所在剽掠，士民避亂，皆入山谷。

translations.literal: Thereupon scattered men of the Six Armies plundered everywhere; soldiers and civilians fleeing disorder all entered the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered soldiers of the Six Armies then looted everywhere; soldiers and civilians fleeing the chaos took refuge in the hills.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，上至陝，百官稍有至者。

translations.literal: On xinsi the emperor reached Shan; a few officials had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the emperor reached Shan, and a few court officials had begun to rejoin him.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀引三十騎自御宿川循山而東，謂王延昌曰：「六軍將士逃潰者多在商州，今速往收之，並發武關防兵，數日間，北出藍田以向長安，吐蕃必遁。」

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi led thirty horsemen east along the mountains from Yusu River and said to Wang Yanchang, "Fleeing and routed soldiers of the Six Armies are mostly at Shangzhou; go quickly now to gather them, and also mobilize the garrison troops at Wu Pass; within a few days, march north out of Lantian toward Chang'an — the Tibetans are sure to flee."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi led thirty horsemen east along the mountains from Yusu River and told Wang Yanchang, "Most of the routed Six Armies soldiers are at Shangzhou — go quickly to rally them and call out the Wu Pass garrison; in a few days we can march north from Lantian on Chang'an, and the Tibetans will surely flee."

sentences.zh: 過藍田，遇元帥都虞候臧希讓、鳳翔節度使高昇，得兵近千人。

translations.literal: Passing Lantian, he met the commander-in-chief's chief adjutant Zang Xirang and Fengxiang military commissioner Gao Sheng and gathered nearly a thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Lantian he met chief adjutant Zang Xirang and Fengxiang commissioner Gao Sheng and gathered nearly a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 子儀與延昌謀曰：「潰兵至商州，官吏必逃匿而人亂。」

translations.literal: Ziyi consulted with Yanchang and said, "When routed troops reach Shangzhou, the officials are sure to flee and hide and the people will fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi said to Yanchang, "When routed troops reach Shangzhou, officials will flee and the people will panic."

sentences.zh: 使延昌自直徑入商州撫諭之。

translations.literal: He sent Yanchang by the direct route into Shangzhou to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yanchang straight into Shangzhou to calm them.

sentences.zh: 諸將方縱兵暴掠，聞子儀至，皆大喜聽命。

translations.literal: The generals had been letting their troops plunder violently; hearing that Ziyi had come, they were all greatly pleased and obeyed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: The generals had been letting their men loot freely; when they heard Guo Ziyi had arrived, they rejoiced and submitted to his command.

sentences.zh: 子儀恐吐蕃逼乘輿，留軍七盤，三日乃行，比至商州，行收兵，並武關防兵合四千人，軍勢稍振。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi feared the Tibetans would press upon the imperial carriage, left troops at Qipan, and only marched after three days; by the time he reached Shangzhou he had gathered troops along the way, and together with the Wuguan garrison they totaled four thousand men, and the army's strength was somewhat restored.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Tibetans might close on the emperor's party, Guo Ziyi held his army at Qipan for three days before moving on. By the time he reached Shangzhou he had rallied troops along the route; with the Wuguan garrison included, he now had about four thousand men, and his force began to recover its footing.

sentences.zh: 子儀乃泣諭將士以共雪國恥，取長安，皆感激受約束。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi then wept and instructed the officers and soldiers that they should together wipe away the nation's shame and recover Chang'an; all were moved and accepted his discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi wept as he addressed his officers and men, urging them to share in redeeming the nation's humiliation and retaking Chang'an. Deeply stirred, they all submitted to his command.

sentences.zh: 子儀請太子賓客第五琦為糧料使，給軍食。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi requested that the Crown Prince's Guest Diwu Qi be made grain supply commissioner to provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi asked that Diwu Qi, a guest of the crown prince, be appointed commissary officer to supply the army with food.

sentences.zh: 上賜子儀詔，恐吐蕃東出潼關，征子儀詣行在。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed an edict on Guo Ziyi; fearing the Tibetans would emerge east through Tong Pass, he summoned Guo Ziyi to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict to Guo Ziyi. Fearing a Tibetan thrust east through Tong Pass, he ordered Guo Ziyi to come to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 子儀表稱：「臣不收京城無以見陛下，若出兵藍田，虜必不敢東向。」

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi submitted a memorial stating: "Your subject, if I do not recover the capital, has no face to meet Your Majesty; if troops are sent out to Lantian, the enemy will certainly not dare to turn east."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi memorialized the throne: "Your servant cannot face Your Majesty unless I retake the capital. If I move troops into Lantian, the enemy will not dare march east."

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 鄜坊節度判官段秀實說節度使白孝德引兵赴難，孝德即日大舉，南趣京畿，與蒲、陝、商、華合勢進擊。

translations.literal: Duan Xiushi, aide to the military governor of Bianfang Circuit, persuaded the military governor Bai Xiaode to lead troops to the emperor's relief; Xiaode that same day launched a major campaign, marching south toward the capital region and joining forces from Pu, Shaan, Shang, and Hua to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiushi, an aide on the staff of Bianfang's military governor Bai Xiaode, persuaded Xiaode to march to the emperor's aid. That very day Xiaode mobilized in force, drove south toward the capital, and combined with troops from Pu, Shaan, Shang, and Hua for a joint advance.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃既立廣武王承宏，欲掠城中士、女、百工，整眾歸國。

translations.literal: After the Tibetans had installed Prince of Guangwu Cheng Hong, they intended to plunder the city's scholars, women, and artisans, assemble their forces, and return home.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they had set up Prince of Guangwu Cheng Hong as a puppet ruler, the Tibetans planned to loot the city's scholars, women, and craftsmen before gathering their army and marching home.

sentences.zh: 子儀使左羽林大將軍長孫全緒將二百騎出藍田觀虜勢，令第五琦攝京兆尹，與之偕行，又令寶應軍使張知節將兵繼之。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi sent the Left Feathered Forest General Zhangsun Quanxu to lead two hundred cavalry out of Lantian to observe the enemy's strength; he ordered Diwu Qi to act as Jingzhao governor and go with him, and also ordered the Baoying Army commissioner Zhang Zhijie to follow with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi dispatched Zhangsun Quanxu, general of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, with two hundred horsemen from Lantian to scout the enemy. He put Diwu Qi in charge of Jingzhao as acting governor and sent him along, and ordered Zhang Zhijie of the Baoying Army to bring up reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 全緒至韓公堆，晝則擊鼓張旗幟，夜則多燃火，以疑吐蕃。

translations.literal: Quanxu reached Hangong Dui; by day he beat drums and raised banners, and by night he lit many fires, to make the Tibetans suspect a larger force.
translations.idiomatic: At Hangong Dui, Quanxu kept up a show of strength by day—drums, banners, and marching—and by night he lit bonfires across the hills to confuse the Tibetans about his numbers.

sentences.zh: 前光祿卿殷仲卿聚眾近千人，保藍田，與全緒相表裡，帥二百餘騎直度滻水。

translations.literal: The former Director of Imperial Sacrifices Yin Zhongqing gathered a force of nearly a thousand, held Lantian, coordinated with Quanxu in inner and outer cooperation, and led more than two hundred cavalry straight across the Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongqing, former director of the imperial sacrificial office, rallied nearly a thousand men and held Lantian. Working in concert with Quanxu, he led more than two hundred horsemen in a dash across the Chan River.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃懼，百姓又紿之曰：「郭令公自商州將大軍不知其數至矣！」

translations.literal: The Tibetans were afraid, and the common people also deceived them, saying: "Commander Guo from Shangzhou is leading a great army of unknown number and has already arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans grew alarmed, and the townspeople fed them a lie: "Commander Guo is marching from Shangzhou at the head of a huge army—no one knows how many—and he is already here!"

sentences.zh: 虜以為然，稍稍引軍去。

translations.literal: The enemy believed it was so and gradually withdrew their army.
translations.idiomatic: Believing the story, the invaders began pulling their troops away.

sentences.zh: 全緒又使射生將王甫入城陰結少年數百，夜擊鼓大呼於朱雀街，吐蕃惶駭，庚寅，悉眾遁去。

translations.literal: Quanxu also sent the archer commander Wang Fu into the city to secretly unite with several hundred young men; at night they beat drums and shouted loudly on Zhuque Street. The Tibetans were terrified and alarmed, and on gengyin they fled with their entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Quanxu also sent Wang Fu, an archer captain, into the city to organize several hundred youths in secret. That night they pounded drums and raised a clamor along Zhuque Street. Panic-stricken, the Tibetans withdrew in full force on gengyin.

sentences.zh: 高暉聞之，帥麾下三百餘騎東走，至潼關，守將李日越擒而殺之。

translations.literal: Gao Hui heard this, led his subordinates of more than three hundred cavalry in flight east, reached Tong Pass, and was captured and killed by the garrison commander Li Riyue.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Hui heard the news, he fled east with some three hundred horsemen. At Tong Pass the garrison commander Li Riyue seized him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔以元載判元帥行軍司馬，以第五琦為京兆尹。

translations.literal: On renchen, an edict appointed Yuan Zai as deputy marshal and army campaign chief of staff, and Diwu Qi as Jingzhao governor.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the emperor ordered Yuan Zai to serve as deputy marshal and chief of staff of the field army, and appointed Diwu Qi governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以郭子儀為西京留守。

translations.literal: On guisi, Guo Ziyi was appointed garrison commander of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Guo Ziyi was made commander of the Western Capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 甲午，子儀發商州。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Guo Ziyi departed from Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Guo Ziyi marched out from Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 巳亥，以魚朝恩部將皇甫溫為陝州刺史，周智光為華州刺史。

translations.literal: On jihai, Yu Chao'en's subordinate general Huangfu Wen was made prefect of Shaanzhou, and Zhou Zhiguang was made prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Huangfu Wen, a subordinate of Yu Chao'en, was appointed prefect of Shaanzhou, and Zhou Zhiguang was appointed prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍、判元帥行軍司馬程元振專權自恣，人畏之甚於李輔國。

translations.literal: The Cavalry General and deputy marshal army campaign chief of staff Cheng Yuanzhen wielded power arbitrarily at will, and people feared him even more than Li Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen, cavalry general and deputy chief of staff to the field marshal, ruled as he pleased, and the court feared him more than it had feared Li Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 諸將有大功者，元振皆忌疾欲害之。

translations.literal: As for generals who had achieved great merit, Yuanzhen envied and resented them all and sought to harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen envied every general of real achievement and looked for ways to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃入寇，元振不以時奏，致上狼狽出幸。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans invaded, Yuanzhen did not report it in timely fashion, causing the emperor to flee the capital in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans invaded, Yuanzhen delayed reporting the crisis, leaving the emperor to flee the capital in confusion.

sentences.zh: 上發詔征諸道兵，李光弼等皆忌元振居中，莫有至者，中外鹹切齒而莫敢發言。

translations.literal: The emperor issued edicts summoning troops from all circuits, but Li Guangbi and the others all resented Yuanzhen's central position, and none came; inside and outside the court all gnashed their teeth yet none dared speak out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called up troops from every circuit, but Li Guangbi and the other great generals resented Yuanzhen's hold on the center and stayed away. Across the empire people seethed with anger, yet no one dared say a word.

sentences.zh: 太常博士柳伉上疏，以為：「犬戎犯關度隴，不血刃而入京師，劫宮闈，焚陵寢，武士無一人力戰者，此將帥叛陛下也。

translations.literal: The academician of the Directorate of Rites Liu Kang submitted a memorial, stating: "The Rong barbarians violated the passes and crossed Long, entered the capital without bloodied blades, looted the palace quarters, and burned the imperial tombs, yet not one warrior fought with all his strength—this is the generals betraying Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kang, an academician in the Directorate of Rites, submitted a memorial arguing: "The barbarians broke through the frontier, crossed Long, and took the capital without a real fight. They plundered the palace and burned the imperial tombs, yet not one soldier stood firm in battle. That means your generals have betrayed you.

sentences.zh: 陛下疏元功，委近習，日引月長，以成大禍，群臣在廷，無一人犯顏回慮者，此公卿叛陛下也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has kept meritorious officials at a distance and entrusted close attendants; day by day the harm has grown until it became a great disaster. Among the ministers at court, not one risked his life to remonstrate—this is the high officials betraying Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: You have pushed aside men of real merit and put your trust in favorites, and day by day that mistake has grown into catastrophe. Not one minister in court has had the courage to speak plainly to your face. That means your chief ministers have betrayed you.

sentences.zh: 陛下始出都，百姓填然，奪府庫，相殺戮，此三輔叛陛下也。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first left the capital, the common people surged forward, seized the treasury, and killed one another—this is the Three Metropolises betraying Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: When you first fled the capital, the people rose in chaos, looted the treasury, and turned on one another. That means the capital region has betrayed you.

sentences.zh: 自十月朔召諸道兵，盡四十日，無只輪入關，此四方叛陛下也。

translations.literal: Since the first day of the tenth month, when troops from all circuits were summoned, through forty days not a single wheel entered the passes—this is the four quarters betraying Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: You called up the armies on the first day of the tenth month, yet in forty days not one unit crossed the passes. That means the empire in every direction has betrayed you.

sentences.zh: 內外離叛，陛下以今日之勢為安邪，危邪？

translations.literal: Inside and outside are divided in rebellion—does Your Majesty consider the situation of today secure or perilous?
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike have turned away from you. Do you think your position today is safe, or in grave danger?

sentences.zh: 若以為危，豈得高枕，不為天下討罪人乎！

translations.literal: If you consider it perilous, how can you rest at ease and not punish the guilty for all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: If you see the danger, how can you sleep easy instead of holding the guilty to account for the whole realm!

sentences.zh: 臣聞良醫療疾，當病飲藥，藥不當病，猶無益也。

translations.literal: I have heard that a good physician treating illness must give medicine suited to the disease; if the medicine does not match the illness, it is still of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled physician treats the sickness at hand with the right medicine. The wrong prescription does no good at all.

sentences.zh: 陛下視令日之病，何繇至此乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty looks at the illness of today—by what cause has it reached this point?
translations.idiomatic: Look at the sickness of the present day. How did it ever come to this?

sentences.zh: 必欲存宗廟社稷，獨斬元振首，馳告天下，悉出內使隸諸州，持神策兵付大臣，然後削尊號，下詔引咎，曰：『天下其許朕自新改過，宜即募士西赴朝廷；

translations.literal: If you must preserve the ancestral temples and the altars of state, cut off Yuanzhen's head alone, dispatch messengers to announce it to all under Heaven, transfer all inner eunuchs to subordination under the circuits, hand the Shence Army over to great ministers, then remove your honorific titles and issue an edict accepting blame, saying: 'All under Heaven, will you permit Us to renew Ourselves and reform Our faults? Let men be recruited at once to go west to the court;
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to save the dynasty, begin by executing Yuanzhen and proclaiming it to the empire. Turn the inner eunuchs out to the provinces, place the Shence Army under senior ministers, renounce your inflated titles, and issue a confession of fault, saying: 'Will the realm allow me to mend my ways? Let loyal men rally at once and march west to the court;

sentences.zh: 若以朕惡未悛，則帝王大器，敢妨聖賢，其聽天下所往。』

translations.literal: If Our wickedness is not yet reformed, then the great vessel of emperorship—we dare not obstruct the sages—let all under Heaven go where they will.'
translations.idiomatic: If my faults remain unreformed, I will not cling to the throne and stand in the way of worthier men. Let the realm choose where its loyalty shall lie.'

sentences.zh: 如此，而兵不至，人不感，天下不服，臣請闔門寸斬以謝陛下。」

translations.literal: If even so troops do not come, the people are not moved, and all under Heaven is not convinced, your subject requests that his entire household be executed by inch-segments to apologize to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Do that, and if the armies still fail to come, the people remain unmoved, and the realm refuses to follow, then let my whole family be put to death inch by inch as my apology to you."

sentences.zh: 上以元振嘗有保護功，十一月，辛丑，削元振官爵，放歸田裡。

translations.literal: Because Yuanzhen had once rendered protective service, in the eleventh month, on xinchou, the emperor stripped Yuanzhen of office and titles and released him to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering Yuanzhen's past service in protecting him, stopped short of execution. In the eleventh month, on xinchou, he stripped Yuanzhen of rank and office and sent him home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 王甫自稱京兆尹，聚眾二千餘人，署置官屬，暴橫長安中。

translations.literal: Wang Fu styled himself Jingzhao governor, gathered a force of more than two thousand, appointed officials, and acted with violence and arrogance throughout Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu proclaimed himself governor of Jingzhao, raised more than two thousand followers, set up a shadow administration, and terrorized Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，郭子儀至滻水西，甫按兵不出。

translations.literal: On renyin, Guo Ziyi reached the west bank of the Chan River, but Fu held his troops and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Guo Ziyi arrived west of the Chan River, but Wang Fu kept his men in camp and refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 或謂子儀，城不可入。

translations.literal: Some told Guo Ziyi that the city could not be entered.
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers warned Guo Ziyi that it was unsafe to enter the city.

sentences.zh: 子儀不聽，引三十騎徐進，使人傳呼召甫；

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi would not listen; he led thirty cavalry forward at an easy pace and sent a man to call out summoning Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi ignored them. With only thirty horsemen he advanced slowly and sent a herald to summon Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 甫失據，出迎拜伏，子儀斬之，其兵盡散。

translations.literal: Fu lost his footing, came out to welcome him and prostrated himself, and Guo Ziyi executed him; his troops all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu, losing his nerve, came out to bow before Guo Ziyi, who had him executed on the spot. His followers scattered at once.

sentences.zh: 白孝德與邠寧節度使張蘊琦將兵屯畿縣，子儀召之入城，京畿遂安。

translations.literal: Bai Xiaode and the Binning military governor Zhang Yunqi led troops stationed at Jixian; Guo Ziyi summoned them into the city, and the capital region was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Xiaode and Zhang Yunqi, military governor of Binning, were encamped at Jixian. Guo Ziyi called them into the city, and order was restored in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 宦官廣州市舶使呂太一發兵作亂，節度使張休棄城奔端州。

translations.literal: The eunuch Guangzhou maritime trade commissioner Lu Taiyi raised troops in rebellion, and the military governor Zhang Xiu abandoned the city and fled to Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Taiyi, the eunuch in charge of Guangzhou's maritime trade office, raised a revolt. Military governor Zhang Xiu abandoned the city and fled to Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太一縱兵焚掠，官軍討平之。

translations.literal: Taiyi let his troops burn and plunder, and government troops suppressed and pacified the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi's men looted and burned at will until imperial forces put the uprising down.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃還至鳳翔，節度使孫志直閉城拒守，吐蕃圍之數日。

translations.literal: The Tibetans returned to Fengxiang; the military governor Sun Zhizhi closed the city and refused to surrender, and the Tibetans besieged it for several days.
translations.idiomatic: On their withdrawal the Tibetans came to Fengxiang. Military governor Sun Zhizhi shut the gates and held out, and they besieged the city for days.

sentences.zh: 鎮西節度使馬璘聞車駕幸陝，將精騎千餘自河西入赴難；

translations.literal: The military governor of Zhenxi, Ma Lin, heard that the imperial carriage had gone to Shanzhou; he led more than a thousand elite horsemen from Hexi to hurry to the rescue;
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Lin, military governor of Zhenxi, learned that the emperor had withdrawn to Shanzhou, he led more than a thousand picked cavalry from Hexi eastward to answer the crisis.

sentences.zh: 轉斗至鳳翔，值吐蕃圍城，璘帥眾持滿外向，突入城中，不解甲，背城出戰，單騎先士卒奮擊，俘斬千計而歸。

translations.literal: Fighting his way in successive engagements he reached Fengxiang, where he found the Tibetans besieging the city. Lin commanded his troops with bows fully drawn facing outward, broke through into the city, did not remove his armor, and with his back to the city wall went out to battle. Riding alone ahead of the soldiers he fought fiercely, capturing and slaying on the order of a thousand before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He fought through to Fengxiang, where the Tibetans were already besieging the city. Lin led his men with arrows nocked and bows drawn outward, burst through the lines into the city, and without doffing his armor sallied from the walls with the city at his back. He spurred ahead of the ranks alone and drove hard at the enemy, capturing and killing nearly a thousand before he came back in.

sentences.zh: 明日，虜復逼城請戰，璘開懸門以待之。

translations.literal: The next day the barbarians again pressed the city and asked for battle; Lin opened the drawbridge gate to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the raiders once more came up to challenge the city. Lin had the portcullis raised and waited for them.

sentences.zh: 虜引退，曰：「此將軍不惜死，宜避之。」

translations.literal: The barbarians withdrew, saying: "This general does not spare his own life—we should avoid him."
translations.idiomatic: They fell back, saying, "This general has no regard for his own life. We had best stay clear of him."

sentences.zh: 遂去，居於原、會、成、渭之地。

translations.literal: They then departed and settled in the regions of Yuan, Hui, Cheng, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Then they withdrew for good and camped in the Yuan, Hui, Cheng, and Wei districts.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁亥，車駕發陝州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dinghai, the imperial carriage departed from Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dinghai, the emperor left Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 左丞顏真卿請上先謁陵廟，然後還宮，元載不從，真卿怒曰：「朝廷豈堪相公再壞邪！」

translations.literal: Left Assistant Minister Yan Zhenqing asked that the emperor first visit the imperial tombs and then return to the palace; Yuan Zai did not agree, and Zhenqing angrily said: "Can the court endure being ruined again by the Chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, left vice minister, urged the emperor to pay his respects at the imperial tombs before returning to the palace. Yuan Zai refused. In anger Zhenqing cried: "Can the court survive being wrecked by you again!"

sentences.zh: 載由是銜之。

translations.literal: Zai therefore bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Yuan Zai nursed a grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 甲午，上至長安，郭子儀帥城中百官及諸軍迎於滬水東，伏地待罪。

translations.literal: On jiawu the emperor reached Chang'an; Guo Ziyi led all the officials and armies in the city to welcome him east of the Hu River, prostrating himself to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the emperor entered Chang'an. Guo Ziyi led the city's officials and garrison troops to meet him east of the Hu River and prostrated himself to accept blame.

sentences.zh: 上勞之曰：「用卿不早，故及於此。」

translations.literal: The emperor consoled him, saying: "I did not employ you early enough, and so things came to this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him, saying: "Had I used you sooner, we would never have come to this pass."

sentences.zh: 以魚朝恩為天下觀軍容宣慰處置使，總禁兵，權寵無比，築城於鄠縣及中渭橋，屯兵以備吐蕃，以駱奉仙為鄠縣築城使，遂將其兵。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en was appointed Inspector-General for Military Affairs and Pacification Commissioner, given command of the imperial guard, and granted power and favor without parallel; he built fortifications at Huxian and Zhongwei Bridge and stationed troops against the Tibetans, appointed Luo Fengxian commissioner for building at Huxian, and thus took command of his troops as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en was made inspector-general of armies and pacification commissioner with overall command of the palace guard. His power and favor were unmatched. He built fortresses at Huxian and Zhongwei Bridge, garrisoned them against the Tibetans, put Luo Fengxian in charge of construction at Huxian, and thereby took Luo's troops under his own command.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以苗晉卿為太保，裴遵慶為太子少傅，並罷政事；

translations.literal: On yiwei, Miao Jinqing was appointed Grand Preceptor and Pei Zunqing was appointed the crown prince's junior tutor, and both were removed from active governance.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Miao Jinqing was made grand preceptor and Pei Zunqing crown prince's junior tutor; both were dismissed from the chief council.

sentences.zh: 以宗正卿李峴為黃門侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Li Kui, director of the imperial clan, was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and co-concurrent chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, director of the imperial clan office, was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 遵慶既去，元載權益盛，以貨結內侍董秀，使主書卓英倩潛與往來，上意所屬，載必先知之，承意探微，言無不合；

translations.literal: After Zunqing departed, Yuan Zai's power grew ever greater; he used wealth to win over the inner attendant Dong Xiu and had chief clerk Zhuo Yingqian communicate with him in secret. Whatever the emperor's intent, Zai always knew it first; aligning with that intent and probing its subtleties, his words never failed to match.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pei Zunqing was gone, Yuan Zai's influence swelled. He bribed the eunuch Dong Xiu and used chief clerk Zhuo Yingqian as a secret go-between. Whatever the emperor had in mind, Zai learned of it first and shaped his replies so that nothing he said missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 上以是愈愛之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore loved him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to favor him even more.

sentences.zh: 英倩，金州人也。

translations.literal: Yingqian was a native of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqian came from Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃既去，廣武王承宏逃匿草野；

translations.literal: After the Tibetans departed, Prince of Guangwu Cheng Hong hid himself in the wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans withdrew, Prince of Guangwu Cheng Hong fled into hiding in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 上赦下誅，丙申，放之於華州。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned the capital punishment decree, and on bingshen he released him at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revoked the death sentence, and on bingshen exiled him to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 程元振既得罪，歸三原，聞上還宮，衣婦人服，私入長安，復規任用，京兆府擒之以聞。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanzhen, having been punished, returned to Sanyuan; hearing that the emperor had returned to the palace, he dressed in women's clothing, secretly entered Chang'an, and again schemed for reappointment. The Jingzhao prefecture captured him and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: After his fall from power Cheng Yuanzhen went home to Sanyuan. When he heard the emperor was back in the capital, he disguised himself as a woman, slipped into Chang'an, and tried once more to regain office. The Jingzhao authorities seized him and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃陷松、維、保三州及雲山新築二城，西川節度使高適不能救，於是劍南西山諸州亦入於吐蕃矣。

translations.literal: The Tibetans captured the three prefectures of Song, Wei, and Bao and two newly built cities at Yunshan; the Xichuan military governor Gao Shi could not rescue them, and so the various prefectures of western Jiannan also fell to the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans took Song, Wei, and Bao and two new fortresses at Yunshan. Gao Shi, military governor of Xichuan, could not relieve them, and the western districts of Jiannan passed into Tibetan hands.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝上之下廣德二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong the Sagely, Cultured, Filial, and Martial — upper fascicle, lower section — second year of Guangde (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong the Sagely, Cultured, Filial, and Martial (lower fascicle), second year of Guangde (

sentences.zh: 甲辰，公元七六四年）

translations.literal: Jiachen, corresponding to 764 CE).
translations.idiomatic: jiachen, 764 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅，敕稱程元振變服潛行，將圖不軌，長流溱州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renyin, an edict stated that Cheng Yuanzhen had changed his dress and traveled secretly, plotting sedition, and he was banished far to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renyin, an edict declared that Cheng Yuanzhen, having disguised himself and moved in secret with treasonous intent, was exiled to distant Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 上念元振之功。

translations.literal: The emperor remembered Yuanzhen's past service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still recalled Yuanzhen's earlier merits.

sentences.zh: 尋復令於江陵安置。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again ordered him settled at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he had Yuanzhen reassigned to Jiangling instead.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，合劍南東、西川為一道，以黃門侍郎嚴武為節度使。

translations.literal: On guimao, Eastern and Western Jiannan Circuits were merged into one circuit, and the vice director of the Chancellery Yan Wu was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Eastern and Western Jiannan circuits were combined into one command, with Yan Wu, vice director of the Chancellery, as military governor.

sentences.zh: 丙午，遣檢校刑部尚書顏真卿宣慰朔方行營。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the acting minister of justice Yan Zhenqing was dispatched to pacify and reassure the Shuofang field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Yan Zhenqing, acting minister of justice, was sent to reassure the Shuofang field army.

sentences.zh: 上之在陝也，真卿請奉詔召僕固懷恩，上不許。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Shaan, Zhenqing requested to be sent with an edict to summon Pugu Huai'en, but the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Shaan, Zhenqing had asked to carry an edict summoning Pugu Huai'en, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，上命真卿說諭懷恩入朝。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor ordered Zhenqing to persuade Huai'en to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor ordered Zhenqing to go and persuade Huai'en to come to court.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下在陝，臣往，以忠義責之，使之赴難，彼猶有可來之理；

translations.literal: He replied: "When Your Majesty was at Shaan, if your subject went and held him to loyalty and righteousness, making him come to the rescue, he still had reason to come.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "When Your Majesty was at Shaan, I could still have gone, appealed to his loyalty, and called him to the emperor's aid. In that situation he might have come.

sentences.zh: 今陛下還宮，彼進不成勤王，退不能釋眾，召之，庸肯至乎！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has returned to the palace; advancing he cannot achieve aiding the throne, retreating he cannot release the masses—summon him, and would he ever come!
translations.idiomatic: But now that you are back in the capital, he cannot advance as a loyal rescuer nor retreat without abandoning his army. Summon him now—why would he ever come!

sentences.zh: 且言懷恩反者，獨辛雲京、駱奉仙、李抱玉、魚朝恩四人耳，自外群臣皆言其枉。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who say Huai'en rebelled are only Xin Yunjing, Luo Fengxian, Li Baoyu, and Yu Chao'en—four men; apart from them all the ministers say he was wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, only Xin Yunjing, Luo Fengxian, Li Baoyu, and Yu Chao'en accuse Huai'en of rebellion. Every other minister in court says he has been wronged.

sentences.zh: 陛下不若以郭子儀代懷恩，可不戰而服也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty would do better to replace Huai'en with Guo Ziyi; without fighting they will submit."
translations.idiomatic: Better yet, put Guo Ziyi in Huai'en's place. The army will submit without a battle."

sentences.zh: 時汾州別駕李抱真，抱玉之從父弟也，知懷恩有異志，脫身歸京師。

translations.literal: At that time the Fenzhou vice-prefect Li Baozhen, a younger cousin of Baoyu on the father's side, knew Huai'en had divergent intentions and escaped to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: About then Li Baozhen, vice-prefect of Fenzhou and a younger cousin of Li Baoyu, realized Huai'en was turning against the throne and fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上方以懷恩為憂，召見抱真問計，對曰：「此不足憂也。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then worrying about Huai'en; he summoned Baozhen and asked his plan, and he replied: "This is not worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, deeply troubled by Huai'en, summoned Baozhen for advice. He replied: "There is no need for alarm.

sentences.zh: 朔方將士思郭子儀，如子弟之思父兄。

translations.literal: The Shuofang officers and soldiers miss Guo Ziyi as sons and younger brothers miss fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang troops long for Guo Ziyi as children long for their fathers and elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 懷恩欺其眾云『郭子儀已為魚朝恩所殺』，眾信之，故為其用耳。

translations.literal: Huai'en deceived his masses, saying, 'Guo Ziyi has already been killed by Yu Chao'en'; the masses believed it, and so they were used by him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en has lied to them, saying 'Guo Ziyi was killed by Yu Chao'en.' They believed him, and that is the only reason they still follow him.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠以子儀領朔方，彼皆不召而來耳。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly puts Ziyi in command of Shuofang, they will all come without being summoned."
translations.idiomatic: If you put Guo Ziyi back in command of Shuofang, they will rally to him without even being called."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，禮儀使杜鴻漸奏：「自今祀圜丘、方丘請以太祖配，祈谷以高祖配，大雩以大宗配，明堂以肅宗配。」

translations.literal: On jiayin, the director of rites Du Hongjian submitted: "From now on, for sacrifices at the Round Mound and Square Mound please use the Great Ancestor as associate; for Praying for Grain use the High Ancestor; for the Great Rain-Prayer use the Great Lineage Ancestor; for the Bright Hall use Emperor Suzong."
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Du Hongjian, director of rites, proposed: "Henceforth, at the Round Mound and Square Mound sacrifices let the Great Ancestor be the associate spirit; at the Praying-for-Grain rite let the High Ancestor be associated; at the Great Rain-Prayer let the Great Lineage Ancestor be associated; and at the Bright Hall let Emperor Suzong be associated."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，立雍王適為太子。

translations.literal: On yimao, Prince of Yong Li Shi was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Prince of Yong Li Shi was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃之入長安也，諸軍亡卒及鄉曲無賴子弟相聚為盜；

translations.literal: When the Tibetans entered Chang'an, deserters from the various armies and local riffraff gathered together as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tibetan occupation of Chang'an, army deserters and local troublemakers banded together as robbers.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃既去，猶竄伏南山子午等五穀，所在為患。

translations.literal: After the Tibetans departed, they still hid in the five valleys such as Ziwu in the Southern Mountains, causing trouble wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the Tibetans left, these men remained hidden in the five valleys of the Southern Mountains, including Ziwu, plaguing the countryside.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以太子賓客薛景仙為南山五穀防禦使，以討之。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the crown prince's guest Xue Jingxian was appointed commissioner for the defense of the five valleys of the Southern Mountains to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Xue Jingxian, a guest of the crown prince, was made commissioner for suppressing bandits in the five valleys of the Southern Mountains.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使田承嗣奏名所管曰天雄軍，從之。

translations.literal: The Weibo military governor Tian Chengsi submitted a request to name his command the Tianxiong Army, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi, military governor of Weibo, asked that his command be named the Tianxiong Army, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩既不為朝廷所用，遂與河東都將李竭誠潛謀取太原；

translations.literal: Since Pugu Huai'en was no longer employed by the court, he then secretly plotted with the Hedong commander Li Jiechen to seize Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from favor at court, Pugu Huai'en secretly joined Hedong commander Li Jiechen in a plot to take Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 辛雲京覺之，殺竭誠，乘城設備。

translations.literal: Xin Yunjing detected it, killed Jiechen, manned the walls, and made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yunjing uncovered the plot, executed Jiechen, and put the city on alert.

sentences.zh: 懷恩使其子瑒將兵攻之，雲京出與戰，瑒大敗而還，遂引兵圍榆次。

translations.literal: Huai'en sent his son Yang to lead troops to attack; Yunjing went out and fought him, Yang was greatly defeated and returned, and then led troops to besiege Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en sent his son Yang against the city. Xin Yunjing marched out to meet him and routed the attack. Yang withdrew and then laid siege to Yuci instead.

sentences.zh: 上謂郭子儀曰：「懷恩父子負朕實深。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Guo Ziyi: "Huai'en and his son have deeply betrayed Us.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Guo Ziyi: "Huai'en and his son have betrayed me utterly.

sentences.zh: 聞朔方將士思公如枯旱之望雨，公為朕鎮撫河東，汾上之師必不為變。」

translations.literal: I hear the Shuofang officers and soldiers miss you as parched drought land hopes for rain; go pacify Hedong for Us, and the troops above Fen will surely not mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: I am told the Shuofang troops yearn for you as drought-stricken fields yearn for rain. Go pacify Hedong for me, and the armies on the Fen will not turn against us."

sentences.zh: 戊午，以子儀為關內、河東副元帥、河中節度等使。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Ziyi was appointed deputy marshal of Guannei and Hedong, Hedongzhong circuit military governor, and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Guo Ziyi was made deputy marshal of Guannei and Hedong and military governor of Hedongzhong, among other posts.

sentences.zh: 懷恩將士聞之，皆曰：「吾輩從懷恩為不義，何面目見汾陽王！」

translations.literal: When Huai'en's officers and soldiers heard this, they all said: "We followed Huai'en in unrighteousness—what face do we have to see the Prince of Fenyang!"
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en's troops heard the news, they said among themselves: "We followed him into wrongdoing. What shame could we show before the Prince of Fenyang!"

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以劉晏為太子賓客，李峴為詹事，並罷政事。

translations.literal: On guihai, Liu Yan was appointed crown prince's guest and Li Kui was appointed household superintendent, and both were removed from active governance.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Liu Yan was made a guest of the crown prince and Li Kui crown prince's household superintendent; both left the chief council.

sentences.zh: 晏坐與程元振交通；

translations.literal: Yan, while out of office, maintained relations with Cheng Yuanzhen;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, though removed from office, kept up ties with Cheng Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 元振獲罪，峴有力焉，由是為宦官所疾，故與晏皆罷。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhen incurred guilt, Kui had a hand in it; for this reason he was hated by the eunuchs, and so both he and Yan were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui had helped bring Yuanzhen down. The eunuchs hated him for it, and both he and Liu Yan were removed from their posts.

sentences.zh: 以右散騎常侍王縉為黃門侍郎，太常卿杜鴻漸為兵部侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: The right regular attendant palace censor Wang Jin was made vice director of the Yellow Gate Department; the minister of rites Du Hongjian was made vice minister of war; both were made co-chief councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, right regular attendant of the Palace Censorate, was appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate Department, and Du Hongjian, minister of rites, was made vice minister of war. Both joined the chief council.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以郭子儀為朔方節度大使。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Guo Ziyi was appointed grand ambassador of the Shuofang field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Guo Ziyi was named grand ambassador of the Shuofang headquarters.

sentences.zh: 二月，子儀至河中。

translations.literal: In the second month, Ziyi reached Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Guo Ziyi arrived at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 雲南子弟萬人戍河中，將貪卒暴，為一府患，子儀斬十四人，杖三十人，府中遂安。

translations.literal: Ten thousand men of Yunnan youth garrisoned at Hezhong; their generals were greedy and the soldiers violent, becoming a scourge to the whole prefecture. Ziyi executed fourteen and had thirty flogged; the prefecture thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Yunnan conscripts garrisoned the city. Their commanders were rapacious and the men unruly, and the whole prefecture suffered for it. Guo Ziyi beheaded fourteen and had thirty flogged, and order returned.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，上朝獻太清宮；

translations.literal: On guiyou, the emperor attended court to offer sacrifice at the Grand Supreme Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor went to court and offered sacrifice at the Grand Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，享太廟；

translations.literal: On jiaxu, he performed the offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，祀昊天上帝於圜丘。

translations.literal: On yihai, he sacrificed to the August Heaven at the Altar of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he sacrificed to Heaven on the round altar.

sentences.zh: 僕固瑒圍榆次，旬餘不拔；

translations.literal: Pugu Chang besieged Yuci but for more than ten days could not take it;
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Chang laid siege to Yuci but could not storm it for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 遣使急發祁縣兵，李光逸盡與之。

translations.literal: He sent messengers to urge the dispatch of troops from Qi county; Li Guangyi gave him all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent urgent messengers to Qi county for reinforcements, and Li Guangyi sent every man he had.

sentences.zh: 士卒未食，行不能前，十將白玉、焦暉緊鳴鏑射其後者，軍士曰：「將軍何乃射人？」

translations.literal: The soldiers had not eaten and could not advance on the march; the subordinate generals Bai Yu and Jiao Hui repeatedly sounded whipping arrows and shot those at the rear. The soldiers said: "General, why are you shooting men?"
translations.idiomatic: The men had not been fed and could barely march. Subordinate commanders Bai Yu and Jiao Hui kept sounding signal arrows and shooting stragglers. The troops cried out, "General, why are you shooting your own men?"

sentences.zh: 玉曰：「今從人反，終不免死；

translations.literal: Yu said: "Now we are following a man in rebellion and in the end cannot escape death;
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yu replied, "We are already following a rebel. Sooner or later we die for it.

sentences.zh: 死一也，射之何傷！」

translations.literal: Death is one—what harm in shooting them!"
translations.idiomatic: Death is death either way. A few more corpses will not hurt!"

sentences.zh: 至榆次，瑒責期遲，胡人曰：「我乘馬，乃漢卒不行耳。」

translations.literal: When they reached Yuci, Chang blamed them for their late arrival; a barbarian said: "We ride horses—it is the Han soldiers who would not march."
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Yuci, Chang rebuked them for being late. One of the non-Han officers said, "We came on horseback. It was the Han soldiers who would not march."

sentences.zh: 瑒捶漢卒，卒皆怨怒，曰：「節度使黨胡人。」

translations.literal: Chang beat the Han soldiers; the soldiers all resented and in anger said: "The military commissioner favors the barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Chang had the Han troops beaten. They seethed with anger. "The commissioner takes the side of the barbarians," they said."

sentences.zh: 其夕，焦暉、白玉帥眾攻瑒，殺之。

translations.literal: That evening, Jiao Hui and Bai Yu led troops to attack Chang and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: That night Jiao Hui and Bai Yu led the men in a surprise attack on Chang and killed him.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩聞之，入告其母。

translations.literal: When Pugu Huai'en heard of it, he went in to tell his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en heard the news and went to tell his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「吾語汝勿反，國家待汝不薄，今眾心既變，禍必及我，將如之何！」

translations.literal: His mother said: "I told you not to rebel. The state has treated you generously. Now that the men's hearts have changed, disaster is sure to reach me—what is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: She said, "I warned you not to rebel. The court has been generous to you. Now the troops have turned, and disaster will surely come to me as well. What are we to do!"

sentences.zh: 懷恩不對，再拜而出。

translations.literal: Huai'en did not reply; he bowed twice and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en said nothing. He bowed twice and left.

sentences.zh: 母提刀逐之曰：「吾為國家殺此賊，取其心以射三軍。」

translations.literal: His mother took a knife and pursued him, saying: "I will kill this traitor for the state and take his heart to display it before the three armies."
translations.idiomatic: She seized a knife and ran after him, shouting, "I will kill this traitor for the empire and cut out his heart to show the army!"
