sentences.zh: 懷恩疾走，得免，遂與麾下三百渡河北走。

translations.literal: Huai'en fled hastily and escaped; he then crossed the Yellow River to the north with three hundred followers and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en ran for his life and got away. With three hundred followers he crossed the Yellow River northward and fled.

sentences.zh: 時朔方將渾釋之守靈州，懷恩檄至，雲全軍歸鎮，釋之曰：「不然，此必眾潰矣。」

translations.literal: At that time the Shuofang general Hun Shizhi was defending Lingzhou. When Huai'en's dispatch arrived, saying that the whole army was returning to the garrison, Shizhi said: "That is not so—this must mean the force has collapsed in rout."
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang officer Hun Shizhi was then holding Lingzhou. When Huai'en's notice arrived proclaiming that the entire army was coming back to its post, Shizhi said, "That cannot be right. The men must have broken and scattered."

sentences.zh: 將拒之，其甥張韶曰：「彼或翻然改圖，以眾歸鎮，何可不納也！」

translations.literal: He was about to refuse them entry when his nephew Zhang Shao said: "They may suddenly change plans and bring the troops back to the garrison—how can we not admit them!"
translations.idiomatic: He was about to shut them out when his nephew Zhang Shao said, "They may yet change their minds and march back under command. How can we refuse to let them in!"

sentences.zh: 釋之疑未決。

translations.literal: Shizhi was doubtful and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi wavered, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 懷恩行速，先候者而至，釋之不得已納之。

translations.literal: Huai'en moved quickly; advance scouts arrived first, and Shizhi had no choice but to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en moved fast. His advance parties arrived ahead of the main body, and Shizhi had no choice but to let them in.

sentences.zh: 張韶以其謀告懷恩，懷恩以韶為間，殺釋之而收其軍，使韶主之；

translations.literal: Zhang Shao informed Huai'en of his plan; Huai'en regarded Shao as a spy, killed Shizhi and took over his army, putting Shao in charge of it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao told Huai'en what he had done. Huai'en treated Shao as a traitor, killed Shizhi, took over his troops, and put Shao in command;

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「釋之，舅也，彼尚負之，安有忠於我哉！」

translations.literal: afterwards saying: "Shizhi was his uncle, and he still betrayed him—how could he be loyal to me!"
translations.idiomatic: then said, "Shizhi was his uncle, and Shao betrayed even him. How could he ever be loyal to me!"

sentences.zh: 他日，以事杖之，折其脛，置於彌峨城而死。

translations.literal: On another day he had him beaten on a pretext, broke his shins, and left him at Miyi city to die.
translations.idiomatic: Later he had Shao flogged on some pretext, broke both his legs, and left him at Miyi to die.

sentences.zh: 都虞候張維岳在沁州，聞懷恩去，乘傳至汾州，撫定其眾，殺焦暉、白玉而竊其功，以告郭子儀。

translations.literal: The chief army supervisor Zhang Weiyue was at Qinzhou. Hearing that Huai'en had fled, he took post-horses to Fenzhou, calmed and settled the troops, killed Jiao Hui and Bai Yu and claimed the credit for himself, and reported to Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chief army supervisor Zhang Weiyue was at Qinzhou. When he learned Huai'en had fled, he rode by post relay to Fenzhou, rallied the troops, killed Jiao Hui and Bai Yu, stole the glory for himself, and reported all this to Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 子儀使牙官盧諒至汾州，維岳賂諒，使實其言。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent his staff officer Lu Liang to Fenzhou; Weiyue bribed Liang to corroborate his account.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent staff officer Lu Liang to Fenzhou. Weiyue bribed Liang to confirm his story.

sentences.zh: 子儀奏維岳殺瑒，傳首詣闕。

translations.literal: Ziyi reported that Weiyue had killed Chang and sent his head to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi reported that Weiyue had killed Chang and forwarded the head to court.

sentences.zh: 群臣入賀，上慘然不悅，曰：「朕信不及人，致勳臣顛越，深用為愧，又何賀焉！」

translations.literal: The officials entered to offer congratulations; the emperor was somber and displeased, saying: "I have failed to trust people as I should and have driven a meritorious subject to ruin. I feel deep shame—what is there to congratulate!"
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers came to congratulate him, the emperor looked grim. "I have been too slow to trust my men," he said, "and a meritorious servant has come to ruin. I am deeply ashamed. What is there to celebrate!"

sentences.zh: 命輦懷恩母至長安，給待優厚，月餘，以壽終；

translations.literal: He ordered Huai'en's mother brought by imperial carriage to Chang'an and provided for with generous care; after a little more than a month she died of old age;
translations.idiomatic: He had Huai'en's mother brought to Chang'an by imperial carriage and treated her with every mark of honor. After a month or so she died peacefully in old age.

sentences.zh: 以禮葬之，功臣皆感歎。

translations.literal: she was buried with full rites, and all the meritorious officials were moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried with full honors, and every distinguished officer was moved.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，郭子儀如汾州，懷恩之眾數萬悉歸之，鹹鼓舞涕泣，喜其來而悲其晚也。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Guo Ziyi went to Fenzhou; the several tens of thousands of Huai'en's troops all returned to him. All cheered, wept, and rejoiced at his coming yet grieved that it was late.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Guo Ziyi went to Fenzhou. Tens of thousands of the men who had followed Huai'en rallied to him. They cheered and wept together, glad he had come and sorry he had come so late.

sentences.zh: 子儀知盧諒之詐，杖殺之。

translations.literal: Ziyi knew of Lu Liang's fraud and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi saw through Lu Liang's deception and had him flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 上以李抱真言有驗，遷殿中少監。

translations.literal: Because Li Baozhen's prophecy had proved true, the emperor promoted him to assistant director of the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Baozhen's warning had proved true, the emperor made him assistant director of the Palace Directorate.

sentences.zh: 上之幸陝也，李光弼竟遷延不至；

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Shanzhou, Li Guangbi in the end delayed and did not come;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew to Shanzhou, Li Guangbi kept putting off his arrival and never came.

sentences.zh: 上恐遂成嫌隙，其母在河中，數遣中使存問之。

translations.literal: The emperor feared that suspicion and rift would form; Guangbi's mother was at Hezhong, and he repeatedly sent palace envoys to inquire after her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared a lasting breach. Guangbi's mother was at Hezhong, and he sent palace envoys again and again to show her care.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃退，除光弼東都留守以察其去就；

translations.literal: When the Tibetans withdrew, Guangbi was relieved of office and appointed eastern capital regent to observe where he would go;
translations.idiomatic: After the Tibetan withdrawal the emperor named Guangbi regent of the eastern capital, the better to see whether he would come or stay away.

sentences.zh: 光弼辭以就江、淮糧運，引兵歸徐州。

translations.literal: Guangbi declined on the grounds of going to oversee grain transport on the Yangzi and Huai, and led his troops back to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi excused himself on the ground of overseeing grain convoys on the Yangzi and Huai and marched his army back to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上迎其母至長安，厚加供給，使其弟光進掌禁兵，遇之加厚。

translations.literal: The emperor welcomed his mother to Chang'an and supplied her generously; he had Guangbi's younger brother Guangjin take charge of the palace guards and treated him with redoubled favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brought Guangbi's mother to Chang'an and lavished gifts on her. He put Guangbi's younger brother Guangjin in command of the palace guard and showed him even more favor than before.

sentences.zh: 戊子，赦天下。

translations.literal: On wuzi, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 自喪亂以來，汴水堙廢，漕運者自江、漢抵梁、洋，迂險勞費。

translations.literal: Since the disorders, the Bian Canal had been choked and abandoned; those transporting grain went from the Yangzi and Han to Liang and Yang by roundabout, perilous routes at great labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebellion the Bian Canal had silted up and fallen into disuse. Grain had to be shipped from the Yangzi and Han to Liang and Yang by long, dangerous detours at enormous cost.

sentences.zh: 三月，己酉，以太子賓客劉晏為河南、江、淮以來轉運使，議開汴水。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiyou, the crown prince's guest Liu Yan was made transport commissioner for the region from Henan and the Jiang and Huai southward, to consider reopening the Bian Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiyou, Liu Yan, guest of the crown prince, was appointed transport commissioner for the lands south of Henan and the Jiang and Huai, with orders to study reopening the Bian Canal.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，又命晏與諸道節度使均節賦役，聽從便宜行畢以聞。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Yan was further ordered, together with the military governors of the various circuits, to equalize and regulate taxes and corvée labor, acting as convenient and reporting when done.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu he was further instructed, together with the circuit military governors, to balance taxes and corvée across the empire, acting as circumstances required and reporting afterward.

sentences.zh: 時兵火之後，中外艱食，關中米斗千錢，百姓挼穗以給禁軍，宮廚無兼時之積。

translations.literal: At that time, after the warfare, court and country alike lacked food; in Guanzhong rice was a thousand cash per dou. The common people rubbed out grain heads by hand to supply the palace guard. The imperial kitchens had not even enough for two meals.
translations.idiomatic: After years of war the empire starved. In Guanzhong a dou of rice cost a thousand cash. Farmers stripped standing grain by hand to feed the palace guard, and the imperial kitchens could not stock even a day's surplus.

sentences.zh: 晏乃疏浚汴水，遺元載書，具陳漕運利病，令中外相應。

translations.literal: Yan then dredged the Bian Canal, sent Yuan Zai a letter setting forth in detail the advantages and drawbacks of canal transport, and had inside and outside the court act in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Yan dredged the Bian Canal, wrote Yuan Zai a detailed account of the costs and benefits of canal transport, and coordinated court and provinces in the effort.

sentences.zh: 自是每歲運米數十萬石以給關中，唐世稱漕運之能者，推晏為首，後來者皆遵其法度雲。

translations.literal: From then on each year several hundred thousand shi of rice were transported to supply Guanzhong. Among those in the Tang praised for ability in canal transport, Yan was ranked first, and those who came after all followed his standards, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter several hundred thousand shi of grain reached Guanzhong every year. Tang historians rank Liu Yan first among masters of canal transport; later generations followed his methods.

sentences.zh: 甲子，盛王琦薨。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Prince Sheng Qi died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Prince Sheng Qi died.

sentences.zh: 党項寇同州，郭子儀使開府儀同三司李國臣擊之，曰：「虜得間則出掠，官軍至則逃入山，宜使羸師居前以誘之，勁騎居後以覆之。」

translations.literal: The Tangut raided Tongzhou. Guo Ziyi sent Li Guochen, honorary grand preceptor of the third rank, against them, saying: "When the barbarians find an opening they sally out to plunder; when government troops come they flee into the mountains. One should put a weak force in front to lure them and strong cavalry in the rear to strike them down."
translations.idiomatic: Tangut raiders struck Tongzhou. Guo Ziyi sent Li Guochen against them with this instruction: "They slip out to loot whenever they see a gap, then vanish into the hills when troops appear. Put a thin screen of men out front as bait and hold your best cavalry in reserve to fall on them from behind."

sentences.zh: 國臣與戰於澄城北，大破之，斬首捕虜千餘人。

translations.literal: Guochen fought them north of Chengcheng, inflicting a great defeat and beheading and capturing more than a thousand of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Guochen met them north of Chengcheng and broke them utterly, killing or capturing more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，癸丑，初行《五紀歷》。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on guichou, the Five Records Calendar was first put into use.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guichou, the court began using the Five Records Calendar.

sentences.zh: 庚申，禮部侍郎楊綰奏歲貢教弟力田無實狀，及童子科皆僥倖；

translations.literal: On gengshen, vice minister of rites Yang Wan memorialized that the annual tribute categories for filial piety and farming had no substance, and that the youth examination was all opportunism;
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Vice Minister of Rites Yang Wan memorialized that the annual quotas for filial sons and diligent farmers were empty formalities and that the prodigy examination was nothing but a shortcut to office.

sentences.zh: 悉罷之。

translations.literal: All were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abolished them all.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀以安、史昔據洛陽，故諸道置節度使以制其要衝；

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi said that because An and Shi had once held Luoyang, military commissioners were placed in the various circuits to control the strategic passes;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi argued that circuit military commissioners had been created to hold the key passes while An Lushan and Shi Siming held Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 今大盜已平，而所在聚兵，耗蠹百姓，表請罷之，仍自河中為始。

translations.literal: Now the great rebels were pacified, yet everywhere troops were massed, draining and harming the common people. He memorialized requesting their abolition, beginning with Hezhong itself.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great rebellion was over, yet armies still crowded every province and bled the people dry. He petitioned to abolish the commissions, beginning at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚辰，敕罷河中節度及耀德軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengchen, an edict abolished the Hezhong military commission and the Yaode Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengchen, an edict dissolved the Hezhong commission and the Yaode Army.

sentences.zh: 子儀復請罷關內副元帥；

translations.literal: Ziyi again requested abolition of the deputy marshalship of Guannei;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi again asked to be relieved of the deputy marshalship over Guannei.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩至靈武，收合散亡，其眾復振。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en reached Lingwu, gathered the scattered and lost, and his troops revived.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en reached Lingwu, reassembled his broken bands, and his force revived.

sentences.zh: 上厚撫其家，癸未，下詔，稱其「勳勞著於帝室，及於天下。

translations.literal: The emperor treated his family generously. On guimwei he issued an edict saying of him: "His meritorious labors were manifest to the imperial house and to the empire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor continued to show his family every kindness. On guimwei he issued an edict declaring, "His services stand recorded in the annals of the dynasty and of the realm.

sentences.zh: 疑隙之端，起自群小，察其深衷，本無他志；

translations.literal: The beginnings of suspicion and rift arose from petty men. Examining his deepest intent, he originally had no other design;
translations.idiomatic: The seeds of mistrust were sown by petty men. Look closely at his heart, and he never meant treason.

sentences.zh: 君臣之義，情實如初。

translations.literal: The righteousness between sovereign and subject remains as at first in feeling and truth.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between ruler and subject is unchanged in spirit and truth.

sentences.zh: 但以河北既平，朔方已有所屬，宜解河北副元帥、朔方節度等使，其太保兼中書令、大寧郡王如故。

translations.literal: But since Hebei is already pacified and Shuofang already has its assignment, he should be relieved of the offices of deputy marshal of Hebei, military commissioner of Shuofang, and the like. His rank as grand guardian, concurrent chief councilor, and Prince of Daining remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: But Hebei is pacified and Shuofang already has its commander. Relieve him of the deputy marshalship of Hebei, the Shuofang commission, and like posts. Let his grand guardian rank, chief councilorship, and title as Prince of Daining stand unchanged.

sentences.zh: 但當詣闕，更勿有疑。」

translations.literal: He need only come to court—let there be no further doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Let him come to court and put doubt aside."

sentences.zh: 懷恩竟不從。

translations.literal: Huai'en in the end did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en still refused.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子，稅天下青苗錢以給百官俸。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengzi, a green-crop tax was levied throughout the empire to pay the salaries of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on gengzi, the court levied a green-crop tax empire-wide to pay official salaries.

sentences.zh: 大尉兼侍中、河南副元帥、臨淮武穆王李光弼，治軍嚴整，指顧號令，諸將莫敢仰視，謀定而後戰，能以少制眾，與郭子儀齊名。

translations.literal: Grand marshal and attendant grand secretary, deputy marshal of Henan, Prince Linhuai the Martial and Solemn Li Guangbi disciplined the army with strict order. At a gesture or a command the generals did not dare look up. He planned before fighting and could use the few to overcome the many; he ranked with Guo Ziyi in fame.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi, Grand Marshal, Palace Secretary, deputy marshal of Henan, and Prince Linhuai the Martial and Solemn, ran an army of iron discipline. At a glance or a shouted order his generals kept their eyes down. He fought only after careful planning and could defeat larger forces with smaller ones. His fame matched Guo Ziyi's.

sentences.zh: 及在徐州，擁兵不朝，諸將田神功等不復稟畏，光弼愧恨成疾，己酉，薨。

translations.literal: When he was at Xuzhou, holding troops and not attending court, generals such as Tian Shengong no longer obeyed in fear. Guangbi, ashamed and resentful, fell ill and on jiyou died.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou he held his army and stayed away from court. Generals like Tian Shengong no longer feared him. Shame and bitterness consumed him until, on jiyou, he died.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙寅，以王縉代光弼都統河南、淮西、山南東道諸行營。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingyin, Wang Jin was made overall commander of the field camps of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East Circuit in Guangbi's stead.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingyin, Wang Jin replaced Guangbi as overall commander of the field camps on the Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀自河中入朝，會涇原奏僕固懷恩引回紇、吐蕃十萬眾將入寇，京師震駭，詔子儀帥諸將出鎮奉天。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi entered court from Hezhong. At the same time Jingyuan reported that Pugu Huai'en was leading one hundred thousand Uyghurs and Tibetans about to invade. The capital was shaken with alarm, and an edict ordered Ziyi to command the generals and go out to garrison Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi came to court from Hezhong just as Jingyuan reported that Pugu Huai'en was marching on the capital at the head of a hundred thousand Uyghurs and Tibetans. Chang'an panicked. The emperor ordered Guo Ziyi to lead the generals out to hold Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 上召問方略，對曰：「懷恩無能為也。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him to ask strategy. He replied: "Huai'en can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his plan. He answered, "Huai'en can do nothing serious."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何故？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why?" the emperor asked."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「懷恩勇而少恩，士心不附，所以能入寇者，因思歸之士耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Huai'en is brave but little bestows favor; soldiers' hearts do not adhere to him. That he can invade is only because of soldiers longing to return home.
translations.idiomatic: "He is brave but never shows grace," Guo Ziyi said. "The men do not love him. They follow him only because they want to go home.

sentences.zh: 懷恩本臣偏裨，其麾下皆臣部曲，必不忍以鋒刃相向，以此知其無能為也。」

translations.literal: Huai'en was originally my subordinate commander; those under his command are all my old troops. They surely cannot bear to turn blades against one another—knowing this, I say he can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was once my junior officer. The troops at his back are still my own old commands. They will not willingly cut one another down. That is how I know he cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 辛巳，子儀發，赴奉天。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Ziyi set out for Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Guo Ziyi marched for Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 甲午，加王縉東都留守。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Wang Jin was additionally made eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Wang Jin was also named regent of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 河中尹兼節度副使崔□發鎮兵西御吐蕃，為法不一。

translations.literal: Hezhong governor and concurrent deputy military commissioner Cui Yu dispatched garrison troops west to resist the Tibetans, but his discipline was inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yu, governor of Hezhong and deputy military commissioner, sent garrison troops west against the Tibetans, but enforced the rules unevenly.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申，鎮兵作亂，掠官府及居民，終夕乃定。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingchen, the garrison troops mutinied, plundering government offices and residents; order was not restored until the night ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingchen, the garrison mutinied and looted government offices and private homes. The disturbance lasted until dawn.

sentences.zh: 丙午，加河東節度使辛雲京同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Hedong military commissioner Xin Yunjing was made co-chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Hedong military commissioner Xin Yunjing was added to the chief council.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以郭子儀充北道邠寧、涇原、河西以來通和吐蕃使，以陳鄭?□舐航躎度使李抱玉充南道通和吐蕃使。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Guo Ziyi was made envoy for reconciliation with Tibet on the northern route from Binning, Jingyuan, Hexi, and beyond; Li Baoyu, military commissioner of Chen-Zheng and Zelu, was made envoy on the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Guo Ziyi was appointed envoy to negotiate peace with Tibet along the northern line from Binning, Jingyuan, and Hexi, and Li Baoyu, commissioner of Chen-Zheng and Zelu, was named envoy on the southern line.

sentences.zh: 子儀聞吐蕃逼邠州，甲寅，遣其子朔方兵馬使晞將兵萬人救之。

translations.literal: Ziyi heard that the Tibetans were pressing Binzhou; on jiayin he sent his son Guo Xi, Shuofang army horse commissioner, with ten thousand troops to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Tibetans were closing on Binzhou, on jiayin Guo Ziyi sent his son Guo Xi, Shuofang cavalry officer, with ten thousand men to its relief.

sentences.zh: 己未，劍南節度使嚴武破吐蕃七萬眾，拔當狗城。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Jiannan military commissioner Yan Wu defeated seventy thousand Tibetans and took Danggou city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Jiannan military commissioner Yan Wu broke seventy thousand Tibetans and captured Danggou.

sentences.zh: 關中蟲蝗、霖雨，米斗千餘錢。

translations.literal: In Guanzhong, locusts and insects and incessant rain—rice was more than a thousand cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts and floods ravaged Guanzhong, and a dou of rice cost more than a thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩前軍至宜祿，郭子儀使右兵馬使本國臣將兵為郭晞後繼。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en's vanguard reached Yilu. Guo Ziyi sent right army horse commissioner Li Guochen with troops as rear reinforcement for Guo Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en's vanguard reached Yilu. Guo Ziyi sent Li Guochen, right cavalry commander, with troops to support Guo Xi from behind.

sentences.zh: 邠寧節度使白孝德敗吐蕃於宜祿。

translations.literal: Binning military commissioner Bai Xiaode defeated the Tibetans at Yilu.
translations.idiomatic: Binning military commissioner Bai Xiaode routed the Tibetans at Yilu.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，懷恩引回紇、吐蕃至晞州，白教德、郭晞閉城拒守。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Huai'en led Uyghurs and Tibetans to Binzhou. Bai Xiaode and Guo Xi closed the city and held out.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Huai'en brought his Uyghurs and Tibetans to Binzhou. Bai Xiaode and Guo Xi shut the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 庚午，嚴武拔吐蕃鹽川城。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Yan Wu took the Tibetan Yanchuan city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Yan Wu captured Yanchuan from the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩與回紇、吐蕃進逼奉天，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en with the Uyghurs and Tibetans advanced to press Fengtian, and the capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en and his Uyghur and Tibetan allies pressed Fengtian, and Chang'an went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 諸將請戰，郭子儀不許，曰：「虜深入吾地，利於速戰，吾堅壁以待之，彼以吾為怯，必不戒，乃可破也。

translations.literal: The generals asked to fight; Guo Ziyi would not allow it, saying: "The barbarians have penetrated deep into our territory and benefit from a swift battle. I will hold the walls and wait for them. They will take me for cowardly and surely will not be on guard—then they can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: His generals begged to attack. Guo Ziyi refused. "The enemy is deep in our country and wants a quick fight," he said. "I will hold fast behind the walls and wait. They will think us timid and drop their guard. That is when we can break them.

sentences.zh: 若遽戰而不利，則眾心離矣。

translations.literal: If we fight rashly and it goes badly, the men's hearts will scatter.
translations.idiomatic: If we rush into battle and lose, the army's heart will break.

sentences.zh: 敢言戰者斬！」

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak of fighting—behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: Whoever urges battle will be executed!"

sentences.zh: 辛未夜，子儀出陳於乾陵之南，壬申未明，虜眾大至。

translations.literal: On the night of xinwei, Ziyi deployed his formations south of Qianling. Before dawn on renshen the barbarian horde arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of xinwei Guo Ziyi drew up his ranks south of Qianling. Before dawn on renshen the enemy host appeared in full force.

sentences.zh: 虜始以子儀為無備，欲襲之，忽見大軍，驚愕，遂不戰而退。

translations.literal: At first the barbarians thought Ziyi was unprepared and intended to strike; suddenly seeing the great army, they were shocked and withdrew without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: They had assumed Guo Ziyi was unprepared and meant to rush him. When the full host materialized they recoiled in shock and withdrew without giving battle.

sentences.zh: 子儀使裨將李懷光等將五千騎追虜，至麻亭而還。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent his deputy generals Li Huai'guang and others to lead five thousand horsemen in pursuit of the barbarians; they reached Mating and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent his lieutenants Li Huai'guang and others with five thousand cavalry in pursuit. They rode as far as Mating, then turned back.

sentences.zh: 虜至邠州，丁丑，攻之，不克；

translations.literal: The barbarians reached Bin Prefecture. On dingchou they attacked it but could not take it;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy reached Binzhou. On dingchou they assaulted the city without success;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，虜涉涇而遁。

translations.literal: On yiyou the barbarians crossed the Jing River and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou they forded the Jing and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 懷恩之南寇也，河西節度使楊志烈發卒萬千，謂監軍柏文達曰：「河西銳卒，盡於此矣。

translations.literal: When Huai'en raided southward, Yang Zhilie, military governor of Hexi, raised ten thousand troops and said to the army overseer Bai Wenda: "The crack troops of Hexi are all here.
translations.idiomatic: During Huai'en's southern raid, Yang Zhilie, military governor of Hexi, mustered ten thousand men and told the army overseer Bai Wenda: "Every elite soldier Hexi can field is in this force.

sentences.zh: 君將之以攻靈武，則懷恩有返顧之慮，此亦救京師之一奇也！」

translations.literal: If you lead them to attack Lingwu, Huai'en will have worry about looking back—this too is one extraordinary stratagem for saving the capital!"
translations.idiomatic: Lead them against Lingwu and Huai'en will have to look over his shoulder—that would be one bold stroke to relieve the capital!"

sentences.zh: 文達遂將其眾擊摧砂堡、靈武縣，皆下之，進攻靈州。

translations.literal: Wenda then led his forces to attack and crush Cuisha Fort and Lingwu County; both were taken. He advanced to attack Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Wenda marched his men against Cuisha Fort and Lingwu County, captured both, and pressed on toward Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷恩聞之，自永壽遽歸，使蕃、渾二千騎夜襲文達，大破之，士卒死者殆半。

translations.literal: Huai'en heard of it, hastened back from Yongshou, and sent two thousand Tibetan and Hun horsemen to night-attack Wenda, routing him greatly; soldiers who died were nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en heard the news, rushed back from Yongshou, and sent two thousand Tibetan and Hun cavalry to strike Bai Wenda by night. The rout was devastating—nearly half his men were killed.

sentences.zh: 文達將餘眾歸涼州，哭而入。

translations.literal: Wenda led his remaining forces back to Liang Prefecture and entered while weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Wenda withdrew what was left of his army to Liangzhou and came through the gates in tears.

sentences.zh: 志烈迎之曰：「此行有安京室之功，卒死何傷。」

translations.literal: Zhilie met him and said: "This expedition had merit in securing the imperial house—what harm if soldiers died?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhilie greeted him and said: "This mission served the dynasty. What does it matter if some men fell?"

sentences.zh: 士卒怨其言。

translations.literal: The soldiers resented his words.
translations.idiomatic: The troops seethed at his remark.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吐蕃圍涼州，士卒不為用；

translations.literal: Before long Tibetans besieged Liang Prefecture, and the soldiers would not be used;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Tibetans besieged Liangzhou, and the troops refused to fight for him;

sentences.zh: 志烈奔甘州，為沙陀所殺，涼州遂陷。

translations.literal: Zhilie fled to Gan Prefecture and was killed by the Shatuo; Liang Prefecture thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhilie fled to Ganzhou, where the Shatuo killed him, and Liangzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 沙陀姓朱耶，世居沙陀磧，因以為名。

translations.literal: The Shatuo bear the surname Zhuye; for generations they dwelt in the Shatuo Desert, and thereby took their name.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo took the surname Zhuye. They had lived for generations in the Shatuo Desert, and from that tract they took their name.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁未，郭子儀自行營入朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingwei, Guo Ziyi entered court from his field camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingwei, Guo Ziyi came to court from his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 郭晞在邠州，縱士卒為暴，節度使白孝德患之，以子儀故，不敢言；

translations.literal: Guo Xi was at Bin Prefecture, letting soldiers commit violence; the military governor Bai Xiaode was troubled by it but, out of regard for Ziyi, dared not speak;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xi was stationed at Binzhou, where he allowed his men to run riot. Military governor Bai Xiaode was appalled but held his tongue out of deference to Guo Ziyi;

sentences.zh: 涇州剌史段秀實自請補都虞侯，孝德從之。

translations.literal: The prefect of Jing Prefecture, Duan Xiushi, volunteered to fill the post of chief military law officer; Xiaode assented.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou prefect Duan Xiushi volunteered for the post of chief law officer, and Bai Xiaode agreed.

sentences.zh: 既署一月，晞軍士十七人入市取酒，以刃刺酒翁，壞釀器，秀實列卒取十七人首注槊上，植市門。

translations.literal: Once appointed for a month, seventeen of Xi's soldiers entered the market to get wine, stabbed the wine-seller with blades, and smashed the brewing vessels. Xiushi lined up the troops, took the seventeen men's heads, spitted them on spears, and planted them at the market gate.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month of his appointment, seventeen of Guo Xi's soldiers went into town for wine, stabbed the vintner, and smashed his equipment. Duan Xiushi had his men decapitate all seventeen and mounted the heads on spears at the market gate.

sentences.zh: 晞一營大噪，盡甲。

translations.literal: One camp of Xi made a great clamor and all donned armor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xi's entire unit erupted in uproar and every man donned armor.

sentences.zh: 孝德震恐，召秀實曰：「奈何？」

translations.literal: Xiaode was shaken with terror and summoned Xiushi, saying: "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Bai Xiaode was terrified. He summoned Duan Xiushi and asked: "What now?"

sentences.zh: 秀實曰：「無傷也，請往解之。」

translations.literal: Xiushi said: "No harm—allow me to go and settle it."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiushi said: "It is nothing serious. Let me go and calm them."

sentences.zh: 孝德使數十人從行，秀實盡辭去，選老躄者一人持馬至晞門下。

translations.literal: Xiaode sent several dozen men to accompany him; Xiushi declined them all, chose one old lame man to hold his horse, and arrived below Xi's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Xiaode offered him an escort of several dozen men. Duan Xiushi refused them all, took only one elderly lame attendant to hold his horse, and rode alone to Guo Xi's gate.

sentences.zh: 甲者出，秀實笑且入，曰：「殺一老卒，何甲也！

translations.literal: Armored men came out. Xiushi smiled as he entered and said: "For killing one old soldier—why armor!
translations.idiomatic: Armed soldiers came out to meet him. Duan Xiushi smiled as he entered and said: "You arm yourselves to kill one old man?

sentences.zh: 吾戴吾頭來矣。」

translations.literal: I have come wearing my own head."
translations.idiomatic: I have brought my own head with me."

sentences.zh: 甲者愕。

translations.literal: The armored men were stunned.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers stood frozen.

sentences.zh: 因諭曰：「尚書負若屬邪，副元帥負若屬邪？

translations.literal: He then addressed them, saying: "Has the Minister wronged you, or has the Deputy Marshal wronged you?
translations.idiomatic: He reasoned with them: "Has Governor Guo wronged you? Has the Deputy Marshal wronged you?

sentences.zh: 奈何欲以亂敗郭氏！」

translations.literal: How can you wish to ruin the Guo clan through disorder!"
translations.idiomatic: Why would you destroy the Guo family's honor by rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 晞出，秀實讓之曰：「副元帥勳塞天地，當念始終。

translations.literal: Xi came out. Xiushi reproached him, saying: "The Deputy Marshal's merit fills heaven and earth—you ought to bear the end in mind as the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xi came out. Duan Xiushi rebuked him: "The Deputy Marshal's achievements fill heaven and earth. Think of what is at stake from first to last.

sentences.zh: 今尚書恣卒為暴，行且致亂，亂則罪及副元帥；

translations.literal: Now the Minister lets his soldiers run violent; soon that will bring disorder, and disorder will bring guilt upon the Deputy Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Your father lets his men run wild. That will soon bring disorder—and when it does, the blame will fall on the Deputy Marshal;

sentences.zh: 亂由尚書出，然則郭氏功名，其存者幾何！」

translations.literal: If disorder arises from the Minister, then how much of the Guo family's fame and achievement will remain!"
translations.idiomatic: If the trouble starts with the Governor, how much of the Guo family's glory will survive!"

sentences.zh: 言未畢，晞再拜曰：「公幸教晞以道，恩甚大，敢不從命！」

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, Xi bowed twice and said: "Sir, you have kindly taught Xi the Way—the favor is very great; I dare not disobey the command!"
translations.idiomatic: Before he could finish, Guo Xi bowed deeply and said: "You have instructed me most kindly. The debt is great—I will not fail you!"

sentences.zh: 顧叱左右：「皆解甲，散還火伍中，敢嘩者死！」

translations.literal: He turned and shouted to those beside him: "All remove armor and disperse back to your fire-teams! Whoever dares make an uproar—death!"
translations.idiomatic: He turned and shouted to his men: "Strip your armor and return to your units! Anyone who raises a clamor will die!"

sentences.zh: 秀實因留宿軍中。

translations.literal: Xiushi thereupon remained overnight in the army camp.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiushi spent the night in the camp.

sentences.zh: 晞通夕不解衣，戒候卒擊柝衛秀實。

translations.literal: Xi all night did not remove his clothes, ordering the watchmen to beat the clappers and guard Xiushi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xi did not undress all night. He ordered the guards to keep watch and protect Duan Xiushi.

sentences.zh: 旦，俱至孝德所，謝不能，請改。

translations.literal: At dawn both went to Xiaode's place, apologized for their inability and asked to reform.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn both men went to Bai Xiaode to apologize and pledge reform.

sentences.zh: 邠州由是無患。

translations.literal: From this Bin Prefecture had no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Binzhou was untroubled from that day on.

sentences.zh: 五穀防禦使薛景仙討南山群盜，連月不克，上命李抱玉討之。

translations.literal: Xue Jingxian, defense commissioner of Wugu, attacked the bandits of the Southern Mountains; for months he could not overcome them. The emperor ordered Li Baoyu to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jingxian, commissioner for the defense of Wugu, had been fighting the bandit gangs of the Southern Mountains for months without success. The emperor ordered Li Baoyu to take over the campaign.

sentences.zh: 賊帥高玉最強，抱玉遣兵馬使李崇客將四百騎自洋州入，襲之於桃虢川，大破之；

translations.literal: The bandit chief Gao Yu was strongest. Baoyu sent the horse-and-army commissioner Li Chongke to lead four hundred horsemen in from Yang Prefecture and surprise them at Taoguochuan, routing them greatly;
translations.idiomatic: The strongest of the bandit leaders was Gao Yu. Li Baoyu sent his cavalry commander Li Chongke with four hundred horsemen from Yangzhou to ambush them at Taoguochuan and broke them utterly;

sentences.zh: 玉走成固。

translations.literal: Yu fled to Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yu fled to Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 庚申，山南西道節度使張獻誠擒玉，獻之，餘盜皆平。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Zhang Xiancheng, military governor of the Western Mountain-South Circuit, captured Yu and presented him; the remaining bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Zhang Xiancheng, military governor of the Western Mountain-South Circuit, seized Gao Yu and sent him to the throne. The remaining outlaws were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙丑，加郭子儀尚書令。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yichou, Guo Ziyi was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yichou, Guo Ziyi was named Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子儀以為：「自太宗為此官，累聖不復置，近皇太子亦嘗為之，非微臣所宜當。」

translations.literal: Ziyi considered: "Since Emperor Taizong held this office, successive sages have not restored it. Recently the crown prince has also once held it—this is not what a lowly subject should accept."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi argued: "Emperor Taizong was the last sovereign to hold this title; no later emperor revived it. Even the crown prince once occupied it. The post is not for a subject such as I."

sentences.zh: 固辭不受，還鎮河中。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and did not accept, and returned to garrison Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused the appointment and returned to his command at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 是歲，戶部奏：戶二百九十餘萬，口一千六百九十餘萬。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Revenue reported: households, a little more than 2.9 million; mouths, a little more than 16.9 million.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Revenue reported 2.9 million registered households and 16.9 million persons.

sentences.zh: 上遣于闐王勝還國，勝固請留宿衛，以國授其弟曜；

translations.literal: The emperor sent the King of Khotan, Sheng, back to his kingdom; Sheng firmly requested to remain in palace guard service and entrusted the kingdom to his younger brother Yao;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the King of Khotan, Sheng, home. Sheng begged to stay on as a palace guard and entrusted his kingdom to his younger brother Yao;

sentences.zh: 上許之，加勝開府儀同三司，賜爵武都王。

translations.literal: The emperor assented, promoted Sheng to honorary third-grade grand master and bestowed the title Prince of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, made Sheng an honorary third-rank grand dignitary, and ennobled him as Prince of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝上之下永泰元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong the Sagely, Cultured, Filial, and Martial — upper fascicle, lower section — first year of Yongtai (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong the Sagely, Cultured, Filial, and Martial (lower fascicle), first year of Yongtai (

sentences.zh: 乙巳，公元七六五年）

translations.literal: yisi, corresponding to 765 CE).
translations.idiomatic: yisi, AD 765).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯朔，改元，赦天下。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the first day guimao, the era name was changed and the empire was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (guimao), the era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 戊申，加陳鄭、澤潞節度使李抱玉鳳翔、隴右節度使，以其從弟殿中少監抱真為澤潞節度副使。

translations.literal: On wushen, Chen-Zheng and Ze-Lu military governor Li Baoyu was added as military governor of Fengxiang and Longyou, and his younger cousin, palace minor inspector Li Baozhen, was made deputy military governor of Ze-Lu.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Li Baoyu, military governor of Chen-Zheng and Ze-Lu, was also made military governor of Fengxiang and Longyou. His younger cousin Li Baozhen, minor inspector of the palace directorate, was appointed his deputy at Ze-Lu.

sentences.zh: 抱真以山東有變，上黨為兵沖，而荒亂之餘，土瘠民困，無以贍軍，乃籍民，每三丁選一壯者，免其租徭，給弓矢，使農隙習射，歲暮都試，行其賞罰。

translations.literal: Baozhen, because there was unrest in Shandong and Shangdang was a military crossroads, and after the desolation of disorder the land was barren and the people distressed with no means to supply the army, then registered the populace: from every three males one strong man was chosen, his rent and corvée were remitted, bows and arrows were given, and in the intervals of farming he was made to practice archery. At year's end there was a capital-wide examination and rewards and punishments were applied.
translations.idiomatic: With Shandong in turmoil and Shangdang on the main military route, Li Baozhen faced a land ruined by war, soil exhausted and people impoverished, with no way to feed his troops. He registered the population and selected one able-bodied man from every three households, exempting him from rent and labor service and arming him with bow and arrows. In the slack season between harvests the men trained in archery; at year's end the whole command was tested and rewards and punishments meted out.

sentences.zh: 比三年，得精兵二萬，既不費廩給，府庫充實，遂雄視山東。

translations.literal: Within about three years he obtained twenty thousand crack troops; since he neither spent granary rations nor depleted supplies, the treasury was full, and he thereupon looked down upon Shandong from a position of strength.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years he had twenty thousand elite troops. Because he did not drain the granaries, his stores stayed full, and he came to dominate Shandong.

sentences.zh: 由是天下稱澤潞步兵為諸道最。

translations.literal: From this the empire called the Ze-Lu infantry the foremost among all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Ze-Lu foot soldiers were reckoned the finest in the empire.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊寅，党項寇富平，焚定陵殿。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuyin, the Tangut raided Fuping and burned the hall of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuyin, Tangut raiders struck Fuping and burned the hall at Emperor Ding's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，儀王璲薨。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Prince Yi Li Lin died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Prince Yi, Li Lin, died.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬辰朔，命左僕射裴冕、右僕射郭英乂等文武之臣十三人於集賢殿待制。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day renchen, thirteen civil and military ministers including left vice director Pei Mian and right vice director Guo Yingyi were ordered to await imperial commands at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day (renchen), thirteen civil and military officials including left vice director Pei Mian and right vice director Guo Yingyi were ordered to stand ready for imperial consultation in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺洛陽獨孤及上疏曰：「陛下召冕等待制以備詢問，此五帝盛德也。

translations.literal: Left remonstrance official Du Guji of Luoyang submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty has summoned Mian and the others to await commands in readiness for consultation—this is the great virtue of the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guji of Luoyang, left remonstrance official, submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has called Pei Mian and the others to stand ready for consultation. That is the virtue of the sage rulers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 頃者陛下雖容其直，而不錄其言，有容下之名，無聽諫之實，遂使諫者稍稍鉗口飽食，相招為祿仕，此忠鯁之人所以竊歎，而臣亦恥之。

translations.literal: Recently Your Majesty, though you tolerated their bluntness, did not record their words. There was the name of tolerating subordinates but not the reality of heeding remonstrance. Thus remonstrators gradually clamped their mouths shut and ate their fill, beckoning one another to offices for salary. This is why loyal and blunt men sigh in private, and your subject is also ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately, though Your Majesty has tolerated blunt counsel, you have not acted on it. You have the reputation of openness but not the practice of listening. Remonstrators have gradually fallen silent, content to draw their salaries and invite one another into office for pay alone. That is why honest men sigh in private—and why I am ashamed as well.

sentences.zh: 今師興不息十年矣，人之生產，空於杼軸。

translations.literal: Now armies have been raised without cease for ten years; the people's production is emptied at loom and spindle.
translations.idiomatic: War has not ceased for ten years. The people's labor is exhausted at the loom and spindle.

sentences.zh: 擁兵者第館亙街陌，奴婢厭酒肉，而貧人羸餓就役，剝膚及髓。

translations.literal: Those who hold armies have mansions stretching across streets and lanes; slaves and maidservants are sated with wine and meat, while the poor, emaciated and starving, go to corvée and skin is flayed to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Men who hold armies live in mansions that line whole streets. Their servants glut themselves on wine and meat, while the poor, gaunt and starving, are pressed into service until flesh is flayed to the bone.

sentences.zh: 長安城中白晝椎剽，吏不敢詰，官亂職廢，將惰卒暴，百揆隳剌，如沸粥紛麻，民不敢訴於有司，有司不敢聞於陛下，茹毒飲痛，窮而無告。

translations.literal: In Chang'an city in broad daylight there is club-robbery; clerks dare not investigate. Offices are chaotic and duties abandoned; generals are lax and soldiers violent. The hundred ministries are ruined and pierced like boiling porridge tangled with hemp. The people dare not complain to the authorities; the authorities dare not report to Your Majesty. They swallow poison and drink pain, destitute with no one to tell.
translations.idiomatic: In broad daylight Chang'an is plagued by robbery, and officials dare not intervene. Government is in chaos, duties abandoned, commanders slack and soldiers brutal. The ministries are in shambles, tangled like hemp in boiling porridge. The people dare not appeal to the authorities; the authorities dare not bring their cries to Your Majesty. They swallow bitterness with no one to hear them.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以此時思所以救之之術，臣實懼焉。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty at this time does not think of the means to save them, your subject is truly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not now devise a way to rescue them, I am truly afraid.

sentences.zh: 今天下惟朔方、隴西有吐蕃、僕固之虞，邠涇、鳳翔之兵足以當之矣。

translations.literal: Now in the empire only Shuofang and Longxi have worry from Tibetans and Pugu; the armies of Bin-Jing and Fengxiang are sufficient to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Today only Shuofang and Longxi face real danger from Tibetans and Pugu Huai'en. The forces at Bin-Jing and Fengxiang are enough to hold them.

sentences.zh: 自此而往，東洎海，南至番禺，西盡巴、蜀，無鼠竊之盜而兵不為解。

translations.literal: From here eastward to the sea, south to Panyu, west through Ba and Shu—there are no rat-thieving bandits, yet the armies are not disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: From there east to the sea, south to Panyu, and west through Ba and Shu, there are no bandits worth the name—yet the armies remain mobilized.

sentences.zh: 傾天下之貨，竭天下之谷，以給不用之軍，臣不知其故。

translations.literal: The goods of the empire are poured out and the grain of the empire exhausted to supply armies that are not needed—I do not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's wealth is poured out and its grain consumed to feed armies with no enemy to fight. I do not understand why.

sentences.zh: 假令居安思危，自可厄要害之地，俾置屯御，悉休其餘，以糧儲屝屨之資充疲人貢賦，歲可減國租之半。

translations.literal: Suppose one dwells in peace yet thinks of danger—one may naturally block the vital passes, station garrisons for defense, and fully rest the remainder, using the resources of grain stores and straw sandals to meet the tax tribute of the weary people; each year the state's land tax could be reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Even in peace one should prepare for danger: hold the strategic passes, garrison what must be held, and stand down the rest. Use the savings from grain stores and straw sandals to ease the people's tax burden, and land tax could be cut by half within the year.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈可持疑於改作，使率土之患日甚一日乎！」

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty hold back in doubt from reform, letting the afflictions of all within the four seas grow worse day by day!"
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty hesitate to act, while the suffering of the realm grows worse with every passing day!"

sentences.zh: 上不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not adopt his advice.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以李抱玉同平章事，鎮鳳翔如故。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Li Baoyu was made co-chief councilor while continuing to garrison Fengxiang as before.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Li Baoyu joined the chief council while remaining military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，吐蕃遣使請和，詔元載、杜鴻漸與盟於興唐寺。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Tibet sent envoys requesting peace. An edict ordered Yuan Zai and Du Hongjian to covenant with them at Xingtang Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Tibet sent envoys seeking peace. The emperor ordered Yuan Zai and Du Hongjian to treat with them at Xingtang Temple.

sentences.zh: 上問郭子儀：「吐蕃請盟，何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Guo Ziyi: "Tibet requests a covenant—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Guo Ziyi: "Tibet wants a peace treaty. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「吐蕃利我不虞，若不虞而來，國不可守矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Tibet profits from our lack of precaution. If they come when we are unprepared, the state cannot be defended."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Tibet thrives on catching us off guard. If they strike when we are not ready, the realm cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 乃相繼遣河中兵戍奉天，又遣兵巡涇原以覘之。

translations.literal: Thereupon in succession he sent Hedong troops to garrison Fengtian, and also sent troops to patrol Jingyuan to observe them.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Hedong troops to garrison Fengtian in succession, and dispatched patrols into Jingyuan to watch the frontier.

sentences.zh: 是春不雨，米斗千錢。

translations.literal: That spring there was no rain; rice was a thousand cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: That spring brought no rain, and rice sold for a thousand cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁丑，命御史大夫王翊充諸道稅錢使。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on dingchou, Censor-in-chief Wang Yi was appointed commissioner for tax money of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingchou Censor-in-chief Wang Yi was made commissioner for circuit tax collection.

sentences.zh: 河東道租庸、鹽鐵使裴諝入奏事，上問：「榷酤之利，歲入幾何？」

translations.literal: Pei Xu, commissioner of rent, corvée, salt, and iron for the Hedong Circuit, entered to report affairs. The emperor asked: "The profit from the liquor monopoly—how much enters each year?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xu, Hedong commissioner for rent, corvée, salt, and iron, came to report. The emperor asked: "How much does the liquor monopoly bring in each year?"

sentences.zh: 諝久之不對。

translations.literal: Xu for a long time did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xu was silent for a long time.

sentences.zh: 上復問之，對曰：「臣自河東來，所過見菽粟未種，農夫愁怨，臣以為陛下見臣，必先問人之疾苦，乃責臣以營利，臣是以未敢對也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked again. He replied: "Your subject came from Hedong. Along the way I saw beans and millet not yet planted; farmers were sorrowful and resentful. Your subject thought that when Your Majesty saw me, you would first ask about the people's hardship and distress, and only then charge me with profit-seeking. For this reason I did not dare answer."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him again. Pei Xu replied: "Coming from Hedong, I saw fields where beans and millet had not even been sown and farmers full of grief and anger. I expected Your Majesty to ask first about the people's suffering before questioning me about profits. That is why I did not dare answer."

sentences.zh: 上謝之，拜左司郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor apologized to him and appointed him left bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor apologized and made him director of the left bureau of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 諝，寬之子也。

translations.literal: Xu was the son of Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xu was the son of Pei Kuan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，劍南節度使嚴武薨。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Yan Wu, military governor of Jiannan, died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Yan Wu, military governor of Jiannan, died.

sentences.zh: 武三鎮劍南，厚賦斂以窮奢侈，梓州剌史章彝小不副意，召而杖殺之；

translations.literal: Wu thrice governed Jiannan, levying heavy taxes to exhaust the people for extravagant luxury. Zhang Yi, prefect of Zizhou, fell slightly short of his wishes; Wu summoned him and had him beaten to death;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu had governed Jiannan three times, squeezing heavy taxes from the people to fund his extravagance. Zhang Yi, prefect of Zizhou, displeased him in a small matter; Yan Wu had him summoned and beaten to death;

sentences.zh: 然吐蕃畏之，不敢犯其境。

translations.literal: Yet the Tibetans feared him and did not dare violate his borders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Tibetans feared him and did not dare cross his borders.

sentences.zh: 母數戒其驕暴，武不從；

translations.literal: His mother repeatedly admonished him against arrogance and violence; Wu would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: His mother repeatedly warned him against arrogance and cruelty, but Yan Wu would not listen;

sentences.zh: 及死，母曰：「吾今始免為官婢矣！」

translations.literal: When he died, his mother said: "I am now at last freed from being an official's bondwoman!"
translations.idiomatic: When he died his mother said: "At last I am free from being the mother of an official's slave!

sentences.zh: 五月，癸丑，以右僕射郭英又為劍南節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guichou, right vice director Guo Yingyi was made military governor of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guichou, right vice director Guo Yingyi was appointed military governor of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 畿內麥稔，京兆尹第五琦請稅百姓田，十畝收其一，曰：「此古什一之法也。」

translations.literal: Within the capital region the wheat ripened. Diwu Qi, metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, requested to tax the people's fields—one tenth collected from every ten mu—and said: "This is the ancient one-in-ten method."
translations.idiomatic: When the wheat ripened in the capital region, Diwu Qi, metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, proposed taxing farmland at one tenth of every ten mu. "This is the ancient tithe," he said."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使侯希逸鎮淄青，好游畋，營塔寺，軍州苦之。

translations.literal: Hou Xiyi, military governor of Pinglu, garrisoned Zi-Qing, loved hunting and touring, and built pagodas and temples; the army and prefectures suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xiyi, military governor of Pinglu, held Zi and Qing. He loved hunting and touring and built pagodas and temples, to the misery of troops and prefectures alike.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使懷玉得眾心，希逸忌之，因事解其軍職。

translations.literal: The horse-and-army commissioner Huaiyu won the hearts of the masses; Xiyi was jealous of him and on a pretext removed his military post.
translations.idiomatic: His cavalry commander Li Huaiyu had won the troops' loyalty. Hou Xiyi envied him and found a pretext to strip him of his command.

sentences.zh: 希逸與巫宿於城外，軍士閉門不納，奉懷玉為帥。

translations.literal: Xiyi lodged with a shaman outside the city walls; the soldiers closed the gates and would not admit him, and installed Huaiyu as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Xiyi was staying with a shaman outside the walls, the soldiers shut the gates against him and proclaimed Li Huaiyu their leader.

sentences.zh: 希逸奔滑州上表待罪，詔赦之，召還京師。

translations.literal: Xiyi fled to Hua Prefecture and submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; an edict pardoned him and summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xiyi fled to Huazhou and submitted a memorial accepting blame. The emperor pardoned him and recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬辰，以鄭王邈為平盧、淄青節度大使，以懷玉知留後，賜名正己。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on renchen, Prince of Zheng Li Miao was made grand ambassador of the Pinglu and Zi-Qing headquarters; Huaiyu was made acting regent, and the name Zhengji was bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renchen Prince of Zheng Li Miao was named grand ambassador of Pinglu and Zi-Qing. Li Huaiyu was made acting regent and given the name Zhengji.

sentences.zh: 時成德節度使李寶臣，魏博節度使田承嗣，相衛節度使薛嵩，盧龍節度使李懷仙，收安、史餘黨，各擁勁卒數萬，治兵完城，自署文武將吏，不供貢賦，與山南東道節度使梁崇義及正己皆結為婚姻，互相表裡。

translations.literal: At this time Li Baochen, military governor of Chengde; Tian Chengsi, military governor of Weibo; Xue Song, military governor of Xiang-Wei; Li Huaixian, military governor of Lulong—they gathered the remnant followers of An and Shi, each holding tens of thousands of crack troops, drilling armies and completing walls, appointing civil and military officers on their own authority, not supplying tribute and tax. With Liang Chongyi, military governor of the Eastern Mountain-South Circuit, and Zhengji they all formed marriage alliances, supporting one another inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Baochen of Chengde, Tian Chengsi of Weibo, Xue Song of Xiang-Wei, and Li Huaixian of Lulong had absorbed the remnants of An Lushan and Shi Siming's forces. Each commanded tens of thousands of elite troops, drilled armies, fortified cities, appointed their own officials, and withheld tribute. They intermarried with Liang Chongyi of the Eastern Mountain-South Circuit and with Li Zhengji, backing one another openly and in secret.

sentences.zh: 朝廷專事姑息，不能複製，雖名籓臣，羈縻而已。

translations.literal: The court devoted itself solely to indulgence and could not again control them. Though called frontier subjects, they were merely tethered in name.
translations.idiomatic: The court could only indulge them and no longer control them. They were called vassal generals in name, but in fact were barely held in check.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以上女昇平公主嫁郭子儀之子暖。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the emperor's daughter Princess Shengping was married to Guo Ziyi's son Nuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the emperor's daughter Princess Shengping was married to Guo Ziyi's son Guo Nuan.

sentences.zh: 太子母沈氏，吳興人也；

translations.literal: The crown prince's mother, Lady Shen, was a native of Wuxing;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's mother, Lady Shen, came from Wuxing;

sentences.zh: 安祿山之陷長安也，掠送洛陽宮。

translations.literal: When An Lushan captured Chang'an, she was seized and sent to the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan took Chang'an, she was seized and sent to the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 上克洛陽，見之，未及迎歸長安；

translations.literal: When the emperor recovered Luoyang he saw her but did not yet bring her back to Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recaptured Luoyang he saw her but had not yet brought her back to Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 會史思明再陷洛陽，遂失所在。

translations.literal: Then Shi Siming again captured Luoyang, and her whereabouts were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shi Siming retook Luoyang, and she vanished without trace.

sentences.zh: 上即位，遣使散求之，不獲。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he sent envoys to search widely for her, but she was not found.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession the emperor dispatched agents far and wide to find her, without success.

sentences.zh: 己亥，壽州崇善寺尼廣澄詐稱太子母，按驗，乃故少陽院乳母也，鞭殺之。

translations.literal: On jihai, the nun Guangcheng of Chongshan Monastery in Shou Prefecture falsely claimed to be the crown prince's mother; upon investigation she proved to be a former wet nurse of the Shaoyang Hall, and was flogged to death.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Guangcheng, a nun at Chongshan Monastery in Shou Prefecture, impersonated the crown prince's mother; when the claim was investigated she turned out to be a former wet nurse of the Shaoyang Hall, and she was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚寅朔，置百高座於資聖、西明兩寺，講仁王經，內出經二寶輿，以人為菩薩、鬼神之狀，導以音樂鹵簿，百官迎於光順門外，從至寺。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day gengyin, a hundred lofty seats were set up at the Zisheng and Ximing monasteries to lecture on the Humane Kings Sutra; from the palace two treasure palanquins bearing the sutras were issued, with people costumed as bodhisattvas and spirits, preceded by musical guard of honor; the hundred officials welcomed them outside Guangshun Gate and followed to the monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day gengyin, a hundred lofty preaching seats were erected at Zisheng and Ximing monasteries for lectures on the Humane Kings Sutra. The palace sent out two jeweled palanquins bearing the sutras, with performers dressed as bodhisattvas and spirits and preceded by a musical guard of honor; officials welcomed the procession outside Guangshun Gate and escorted it to the temples.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩誘回紇、吐蕃、吐谷渾、党項、奴剌數十萬眾俱入寇，令吐蕃大將尚結悉贊磨、馬重英等自北道趣奉天，党項帥任敷、鄭庭、郝德等自東道趣同州，吐谷渾、奴剌之眾自西道趣盩厔，回紇繼吐蕃之後，懷恩又以朔方兵繼之。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en incited the Uyghurs, Tibetans, Tuyuhun, Tangut, and Nula — several hundred thousand in all — to invade together. He ordered the Tibetan generals Shang Jiesi Zanmo, Ma Chongying, and others to advance by the northern route toward Fengtian; the Tangut chiefs Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, Hao De, and others by the eastern route toward Tong Prefecture; the Tuyuhun and Nula forces by the western route toward Zhouzhi; the Uyghurs following the Tibetans, and Huai'en with Shuofang troops following them.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en persuaded the Uyghurs, Tibetans, Tuyuhun, Tangut, and Nula — several hundred thousand men in all — to raid together. He sent the Tibetan generals Shang Jiesi Zanmo and Ma Chongying by the northern route toward Fengtian; the Tangut chiefs Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, and Hao De by the eastern route toward Tong Prefecture; the Tuyuhun and Nula by the western route toward Zhouzhi; the Uyghurs followed the Tibetans, and Huai'en brought up the rear with Shuofang troops.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀使行軍司馬趙復入奏曰：「虜皆騎兵，其來如飛，不可易也。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi sent his marching staff officer Zhao Fu to enter and memorialize, saying: "The barbarians are all cavalry; they come like flight — they must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent his chief of staff Zhao Fu to court with a memorial: "The enemy is all cavalry; they will arrive like a wind — we must not underestimate them.

sentences.zh: 請使諸道節度使鳳翔李抱玉、滑濮李光庭、邠寧白孝德、鎮西馬璘、河南郝庭玉、淮西李忠臣各出兵以扼其衝要。」

translations.literal: Please order the military commissioners of the various circuits — Li Baoyu of Fengxiang, Li Guangting of Hua-Pu, Bai Xiaode of Binning, Ma Lin of Zhenxi, Hao Tingyu of Henan, Li Zhongchen of Huai-Hsi — each to send out troops to block their strategic points."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the circuit commissioners be ordered to march — Li Baoyu of Fengxiang, Li Guangting of Hua-Pu, Bai Xiaode of Binning, Ma Lin of Zhenxi, Hao Tingyu of Henan, and Li Zhongchen of Huai-Hsi — each to deploy troops and hold the enemy's vital passes."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 諸道多不時出兵；

translations.literal: Many circuits did not send troops on time;
translations.idiomatic: Most circuits failed to march promptly;

sentences.zh: 李忠臣方與諸將擊球，得詔，亟命治行。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchen was just playing cuju ball with his generals; receiving the edict, he at once ordered preparations to march.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen was in the middle of a cuju match with his generals when the edict arrived; he immediately ordered his men to prepare to march.

sentences.zh: 諸將及監軍皆曰：「師行必擇日。」

translations.literal: The generals and army monitors all said: "When an army sets out, one must choose an auspicious day."
translations.idiomatic: The generals and army supervisors all protested: "An army must choose an auspicious day before setting out."

sentences.zh: 忠臣怒曰：「父母有急，豈可擇日而後救邪！」

translations.literal: Zhongchen angrily said: "When one's parents are in peril, how can one choose a day before going to save them!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen snapped: "When your parents are in danger, do you pick a lucky day before you go to save them!"

sentences.zh: 即日勒兵就道。

translations.literal: That very day he mustered troops and set out on the march.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he mustered his troops and took the road.

sentences.zh: 懷恩中途遇暴疾而歸；

translations.literal: Huai'en, en route, was struck by a sudden illness and returned;
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en fell gravely ill on the march and turned back;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，死於鳴沙。

translations.literal: On dingyou he died at Mingsha.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he died at Mingsha.

sentences.zh: 大將張韶代領其眾，別將徐璜玉殺之，范志誠又殺璜玉而領其眾。

translations.literal: The great general Zhang Shao took command of his forces in his stead; the lieutenant Xu Huangyu killed him, and Fan Zhicheng killed Huangyu and took command of the forces.
translations.idiomatic: The senior general Zhang Shao assumed command of his army; the deputy Xu Huangyu killed him, and Fan Zhicheng then killed Huangyu and seized command in turn.

sentences.zh: 懷恩拒命三年，再引胡寇，為國大患，上猶為之隱，前後制敕未嘗言其反；

translations.literal: Huai'en had defied orders for three years and twice led barbarian raiders — a great calamity for the state — yet the emperor still concealed his treason; edicts before and after never spoke of his rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en had defied the throne for three years and twice brought barbarian armies against the empire, yet the emperor still shielded him: no edict before or since ever called it rebellion;

sentences.zh: 及聞其死，憫然曰：「懷恩不反，為左右所誤耳！」

translations.literal: When he heard of his death, he said mournfully: "Huai'en did not rebel — he was misled by those around him!"
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death reached the emperor, he said with sorrow: "Huai'en never meant to rebel — his advisers led him astray!

sentences.zh: 吐蕃至邠州，白孝德嬰城自守。

translations.literal: The Tibetans reached Bin Prefecture; Bai Xiaode closed the city and held it himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans reached Bin Prefecture; Bai Xiaode shut the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，上命宰相及諸司長官於西明寺行香設素饌，奏樂。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the emperor ordered chancellors and directors of the various bureaus to burn incense and set out vegetarian fare at Ximing Monastery, with music performed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the emperor ordered the chancellors and bureau heads to burn incense and serve a vegetarian meal at Ximing Monastery, with music.

sentences.zh: 是日，吐蕃十萬眾至奉天，京城震恐。

translations.literal: That day a hundred thousand Tibetans reached Fengtian, and the capital was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: That day a hundred thousand Tibetans reached Fengtian, and the capital was convulsed with fear.

sentences.zh: 朔方兵馬使渾瑊、討擊使白元光先戍奉天，虜始列營，瑊帥驍騎二百直衝之，身先士卒，虜眾披靡。

translations.literal: Hun Jian, horse commissioner of the Shuofang army, and Bai Yuanguang, strike commissioner, were already garrisoned at Fengtian. When the barbarians first formed camp, Jian led two hundred crack cavalry in a direct charge, taking the lead before his soldiers; the barbarian host was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian, Shuofang cavalry commissioner, and Bai Yuanguang, strike commissioner, were already stationed at Fengtian. When the enemy first pitched camp, Jian led two hundred elite horsemen in a headlong charge at the front of his men, and the barbarian ranks broke and scattered.

sentences.zh: 瑊挾虜將一人躍馬而還，從騎無中鋒鏑者。

translations.literal: Jian seized one barbarian general under his arm and leapt back on horseback; none of the escort horsemen were struck by enemy arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Jian grabbed a barbarian officer, tucked him under his arm, and galloped back; not one of his escort took an arrow.

sentences.zh: 城上士卒望之，勇氣始振。

translations.literal: The soldiers on the wall saw this, and their courage was first roused.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders on the walls saw it, and their spirits rose for the first time.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，吐蕃進攻之，虜死傷甚眾，數日，斂眾還營；

translations.literal: On yisi the Tibetans pressed the attack; very many barbarians were killed and wounded; after several days they gathered their forces and withdrew to camp;
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Tibetans pressed the assault; enemy dead and wounded were very heavy; after several days they drew off and returned to camp;

sentences.zh: 瑊夜引兵襲之，殺千餘人，前後與虜戰二百餘合，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: Jian by night led troops to raid them, killing more than a thousand; before and after he fought more than two hundred engagements with the barbarians, beheading five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jian led a night raid that killed more than a thousand; in over two hundred clashes with the enemy before and after, he took five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 丙午，罷百高座講；

translations.literal: On bingwu, the hundred-lofty-seat lectures were discontinued;
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the hundred-seat sutra lectures were suspended;

sentences.zh: 召郭子儀於河中，使屯涇陽。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi was summoned from Hezhong and ordered to encamp at Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was recalled from Hezhong and ordered to encamp at Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 己酉，命李忠臣屯東渭橋，李光進屯雲陽，馬璘、郝庭玉屯便橋，李抱玉屯鳳翔，內侍駱奉仙、將軍李日越屯盩厔，同華節度使周智光屯同州，鄜坊節度使杜冕屯坊州，上自將六軍屯苑中。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Li Zhongchen was ordered to encamp at East Wei Bridge, Li Guangjin at Yunyang, Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Bian Bridge, Li Baoyu at Fengxiang, the palace eunuch Luo Fengxian and general Li Riyue at Zhouzhi, Tong-Hua commissioner Zhou Zhiguang at Tong Prefecture, Yingfang commissioner Du Mian at Fang Prefecture, and the emperor personally led the Six Armies to encamp in the palace park.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Li Zhongchen was posted at East Wei Bridge, Li Guangjin at Yunyang, Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Bian Bridge, Li Baoyu at Fengxiang, the palace eunuch Luo Fengxian and general Li Riyue at Zhouzhi, Tong-Hua commissioner Zhou Zhiguang at Tong Prefecture, Yingfang commissioner Du Mian at Fang Prefecture, and the emperor himself led the Six Armies into camp within the palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，下制親征。

translations.literal: On gengxu, an edict was issued announcing the emperor's personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu an edict declared that the emperor would take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魚朝恩請索城中，括士民私馬，令城中男子皆衣皁，團結為兵，城門皆塞二開一。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Yu Chaoen requested a search of the city to requisition private horses from gentry and commoners, ordered all men in the city to wear black garments and be organized into militia, and that city gates be blocked two-thirds open one-third.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Yu Chaoen proposed searching the city and seizing private horses from citizens, ordering every man to wear black and be mustered as militia, and leaving each gate two-thirds barred and one-third open.

sentences.zh: 士民大駭，逾垣鑿竇而逃者甚眾，吏不能禁。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners were greatly terrified; very many climbed walls and dug holes to flee, and officials could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Citizens were terrified; crowds scaled walls and dug through barriers to escape, and the authorities could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 朝恩欲奉上幸河中以避吐蕃，恐群臣論議不一；

translations.literal: Chaoen wished to have the emperor go to Hezhong to avoid the Tibetans, but feared the officials would not agree in debate;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen wanted the emperor to move to Hezhong to escape the Tibetans, but feared the court would not fall in line;

sentences.zh: 一旦百官入朝，立班久之，閣門不開，朝恩忽從禁軍十餘人操白刃而出，宣言：「吐蕃數犯郊畿，車駕欲幸河中，何如？」

translations.literal: One morning when the hundred officials entered court, they stood in formation for a long time and the gate of the privy chamber did not open. Chaoen suddenly emerged with more than ten armored-guard soldiers bearing naked blades and proclaimed: "The Tibetans have repeatedly violated the capital suburbs; the imperial carriage wishes to go to Hezhong — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: One morning the officials entered court and stood waiting a long time, but the privy chamber gate never opened. Chaoen suddenly appeared with a dozen armored guards bearing naked blades and announced: "The Tibetans have struck the capital suburbs again; the emperor wishes to go to Hezhong — what say you?"

sentences.zh: 公卿皆錯愕不知所對。

translations.literal: The ministers and high officials were all stunned and did not know how to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers were stunned and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 有劉給事者，獨出班抗聲曰：「敕使反邪！

translations.literal: There was Attendant Liu, who alone stepped from the ranks and cried out: "Commissioner, do you rebel!
translations.idiomatic: One attendant, Liu, stepped alone from the ranks and shouted: "Commissioner — are you in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 今屯軍如雲，不戮力扞寇，而遽欲脅天子棄宗廟社稷而去，非反而何！」

translations.literal: Now our armies mass as thick as clouds — rather than join forces to repel the invaders, you would suddenly coerce the Son of Heaven to abandon the ancestral temples and altar of soil and flee! What is this if not rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Our armies stand massed like clouds, yet instead of uniting to beat back the invaders you would coerce the Son of Heaven to abandon the ancestral temples and the realm — if that is not treason, what is!"

sentences.zh: 朝恩驚沮而退，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Chaoen was startled and discouraged and withdrew; the matter then came to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen, shaken, withdrew, and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 自丙午至甲寅，大雨不止，故虜不能進。

translations.literal: From bingwu to jiayin, heavy rain fell without cease, and therefore the barbarians could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: From bingwu through jiayin torrential rain never let up, and the enemy could not advance.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃移兵攻醴泉，党項西掠白水，東侵蒲津。

translations.literal: The Tibetans shifted troops to attack Liquan; the Tangut raided west at Baishui and east invaded Pu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans redeployed to attack Liquan; the Tangut plundered Baishui in the west and struck east at Pu Ford.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，吐蕃大掠男女數萬而去，所過焚廬舍，蹂禾嫁殆盡。

translations.literal: On dingsi the Tibetans plundered several tens of thousands of men and women and departed; wherever they passed they burned dwellings and trampled the grain crops nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Tibetans carried off tens of thousands of men and women and withdrew, burning houses along their route and trampling the harvest nearly bare.

sentences.zh: 周智光引兵邀擊，破之於澄城北，因逐北至邠州。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhiguang led troops to intercept and attack them, defeating them north of Chen Prefecture, then pursued them north to Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhiguang intercepted them, routed them north of Chen Prefecture, and pursued them as far as Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 智光素與杜冕不協，遂殺鄜州剌史張麟，坑冕家屬八十一人，焚坊州廬舍三千餘家。

translations.literal: Zhiguang had long been at odds with Du Mian; he then killed Yong Prefecture prefect Zhang Lin, buried alive eighty-one of Mian's family members, and burned more than three thousand dwellings at Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang had long been at odds with Du Mian; he killed Yong Prefecture prefect Zhang Lin, buried alive eighty-one members of Mian's household, and burned more than three thousand homes in Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己未，復講經於資聖寺。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei, sutra lectures were resumed at Zisheng Monastery.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei, sutra lectures resumed at Zisheng Monastery.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃退至邠州，遇回紇，復相與入寇，辛酉，至奉天。

translations.literal: The Tibetans withdrew to Bin Prefecture, met the Uyghurs, and again joined with them to invade; on xinyou they reached Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans fell back to Bin Prefecture, joined forces with the Uyghurs, and raided again; on xinyou they reached Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，党項焚同州官廨、民居而去。

translations.literal: On guihai the Tangut burned the official halls and commoners' dwellings at Tong Prefecture and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the Tangut burned Tong Prefecture's government offices and private homes and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，回紇、吐蕃合兵圍涇陽，子儀命諸將嚴設守備而不戰。

translations.literal: On bingyin the Uyghurs and Tibetans combined forces to surround Jingyang; Ziyi ordered his generals to set strict defenses and not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Uyghurs and Tibetans joined to besiege Jingyang; Ziyi ordered his generals to fortify the defenses and hold their fire.

sentences.zh: 及幕，二虜退屯北原，丁卯，復至城下。

translations.literal: At dusk the two barbarian hosts withdrew and encamped on the North Plain; on dingmao they again came below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk both enemy armies withdrew to camp on the North Plain; on dingmao they returned beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 是時，回紇與吐蕃聞僕固懷恩死，已爭長，不相睦，分營而居，子儀知之。

translations.literal: At this time the Uyghurs and Tibetans, hearing that Pugu Huai'en was dead, were already contending for precedence and were not on good terms; they encamped separately. Ziyi knew this.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Uyghurs and Tibetans, learning of Pugu Huai'en's death, were already quarreling over precedence and encamped apart; Ziyi knew it.

sentences.zh: 回紇在城西，子儀使牙將李光瓚等往說之，欲與之共擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs were west of the city; Ziyi sent his yamen general Li Guangzan and others to go persuade them, wishing to join with them in attacking the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were camped west of the city; Ziyi sent his staff officer Li Guangzan and others to win them over and propose a joint strike against the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 回紇不信，曰：「郭公固在此乎？

translations.literal: The Uyghurs did not believe it and said: "Is Duke Guo really here?
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs did not believe him and said: "Is Duke Guo really here?

sentences.zh: 汝紿我耳。

translations.literal: You deceive us.
translations.idiomatic: You are lying to us.

sentences.zh: 若果在此，可得見乎？」

translations.literal: If he is really here, can we see him?"
translations.idiomatic: If he truly is here, may we see him?"

sentences.zh: 光瓚還報，子儀曰：「今眾寡不敵，難以力勝。

translations.literal: Guangzan returned to report; Ziyi said: "Now we are too few to match them — hard to win by force.
