translations.idiomatic: Guangzan returned with their answer; Ziyi said: "We are too few to match them — force will not prevail.

sentences.zh: 昔與回紇契約甚厚，不若挺身往說之，可不戰而下也。」

translations.literal: Formerly our covenant with the Uyghurs was very close; better to go in person bare-bodied to persuade them — we may make them withdraw without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Our old bond with the Uyghurs runs deep; better I go alone and speak to them face to face — we may win them over without a battle."

sentences.zh: 諸將請選鐵騎五百為衛從，子儀曰：「此適足為害也。」

translations.literal: The generals asked to select five hundred iron cavalry as escort; Ziyi said: "That would be just enough to do harm."
translations.idiomatic: The generals offered five hundred armored horsemen as escort; Ziyi said: "That would only make things worse."

sentences.zh: 郭晞扣馬諫曰：「彼，虎狼也；

translations.literal: Guo Xi seized his horse's bridle and remonstrated, saying: "They are tigers and wolves;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xi caught his bridle and pleaded: "They are wolves;

sentences.zh: 大人，國之元帥，奈何以身為虜餌！」

translations.literal: Father, you are the nation's commander-in-chief — how can you offer your own body as bait for the barbarians!"
translations.idiomatic: Father, you are the empire's commander-in-chief — how can you offer yourself as bait to the barbarians!"

sentences.zh: 子儀曰：「今戰，則父子俱死而國家危；

translations.literal: Ziyi said: "If we fight now, then father and son will both die and the state will be in peril;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi replied: "If we fight now, father and son die together and the realm is lost;

sentences.zh: 往以至誠與之言，或幸而見從，則四海之福也！

translations.literal: If I go and speak to them with utmost sincerity, perhaps by fortune they will consent — that would be fortune for the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: If I go and speak with complete sincerity, perhaps they will listen — that would be a blessing for the whole empire!

sentences.zh: 不然，則身沒而家全。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, my person perishes but the family is preserved."
translations.idiomatic: If not, I die alone and the house survives."

sentences.zh: 以鞭擊其手曰：「去！」

translations.literal: He struck his hand with a whip and said: "Go!"
translations.idiomatic: He lashed his hand with the whip and cried: "Away!"

sentences.zh: 遂與數騎開門而出，使人傳呼曰：「令公來！」

translations.literal: Thereupon with several horsemen he opened the gate and went out; men were sent to call out: "The Duke comes!"
translations.idiomatic: Then, with only a few horsemen, he opened the gate and rode out; heralds cried: "The Duke is coming!"

sentences.zh: 回紇大驚。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were stunned.

sentences.zh: 其大帥合胡祿都督藥葛羅，可汗之弟也，執弓注矢立於陣前。

translations.literal: Their great chief Heluhulu Tutuqu Yaogeluo, the qaghan's younger brother, nocked an arrow to his bow and stood before the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader, Heluhulu Tutuqu Yaogeluo, the qaghan's younger brother, stood at the front of the line with bow drawn and arrow nocked.

sentences.zh: 子儀免冑釋甲投槍而進，回紇諸酋長相顧曰：「是也！」

translations.literal: Ziyi removed his helmet, doffed his armor, and cast aside his spear as he advanced; the Uyghur chieftains looked at one another and said: "It is he!"
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi doffed helmet and armor, cast aside his spear, and walked forward; the Uyghur chiefs looked at one another and exclaimed: "It is he!"

sentences.zh: 皆下馬羅拜。

translations.literal: All dismounted and prostrated themselves in rows.
translations.idiomatic: All dismounted and bowed to the ground in ranks.

sentences.zh: 子儀亦下馬，前執藥葛羅手，讓之曰：「汝回紇有大功於唐，唐之報汝亦不薄，奈何負約，深入吾地，侵逼畿縣，棄前功，結怨仇，背恩德而助叛臣，何其愚也！

translations.literal: Ziyi also dismounted, went forward and took Yaogeluo by the hand, and reproached him, saying: "You Uyghurs rendered great merit to Tang, and Tang's repayment to you has not been meager — why break the covenant, penetrate deep into our territory, press upon the capital counties, abandon former merit, tie on enmity and hatred, turn your back on grace and virtue to aid a rebel minister — how foolish!
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi dismounted too, took Yaogeluo by the hand, and rebuked him: "Your Uyghurs have served Tang with great merit, and Tang has repaid you generously — why break your oath, march deep into our land, press on the capital counties, throw away past glory, make enemies, turn against kindness, and help a rebel minister? How foolish!

sentences.zh: 且懷恩叛君棄母，於汝國何有！

translations.literal: Moreover Huai'en rebelled against his lord and abandoned his mother — what did he mean to your country!
translations.idiomatic: And Huai'en betrayed his sovereign and abandoned his mother — what was that to your nation!

sentences.zh: 今吾挺身而來，聽汝執我殺之，我之將士必致死與汝戰矣。」

translations.literal: Now I have come bare-bodied; heed if you will seize me and kill me — my generals and soldiers will surely fight you to the death."
translations.idiomatic: Now I have come unarmed; if you seize me and kill me, my officers and men will fight you to the death."

sentences.zh: 藥葛羅曰：「懷恩欺我，言天可汗已晏駕，令公亦捐館，中國無主，我是以敢與之來。

translations.literal: Yaogeluo said: "Huai'en deceived us, saying the Heavenly Qaghan had already passed away and the Duke had also died, and that China had no ruler — therefore we dared come with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yaogeluo said: "Huai'en deceived us, claiming the Heavenly Qaghan was dead, that you too had perished, and that China had no master — that is why we dared march with him.

sentences.zh: 今知天可汗在上都，令公復總兵於此，懷恩又為天所殺，我曹豈肯與令公戰乎！」

translations.literal: Now we know the Heavenly Qaghan is at the Upper Capital and the Duke again commands troops here; Huai'en has also been killed by Heaven — how could we be willing to fight the Duke!"
translations.idiomatic: Now we know the Heavenly Qaghan is at the Upper Capital and you command troops here again; Heaven has already taken Huai'en — why would we fight you!"

sentences.zh: 子儀因說之曰：「吐蕃無道，乘我國有亂，不顧舅甥之親，吞噬我邊鄙，焚蕩我畿甸，其所掠之財不可勝載，馬牛雜畜，長數百里，彌溫在野，此天以賜汝也。

translations.literal: Ziyi therefore persuaded him, saying: "The Tibetans are without the Way; taking advantage of our state's disorder, heedless of the uncle-nephew bond, they swallowed our border lands, burned and swept our capital region — the wealth they plundered cannot be fully loaded; horses, cattle, and mixed livestock stretch for hundreds of li, filling the fields warm with life — this Heaven bestows upon you.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi pressed on: "The Tibetans are lawless; they seized our disorder, ignored the uncle-nephew bond, swallowed our frontiers, and burned the capital region. The loot they carry countless; horses and cattle stretch for hundreds of li across the fields — Heaven has put this in your hands.

sentences.zh: 全師而繼好，破敵以取富，為汝計，孰便於此！

translations.literal: To keep your army intact and renew friendship, smash the enemy and take riches — for your reckoning, what is more convenient than this!
translations.idiomatic: Keep your army whole, renew the friendship, crush the enemy, and take the wealth — for you, what bargain could be better!

sentences.zh: 不可失也。」

translations.literal: You must not lose it."
translations.idiomatic: Do not let it slip away."

sentences.zh: 藥葛羅曰：「吾為懷恩所誤，負公誠深，今請為公盡力，擊吐蕃以謝過。

translations.literal: Yaogeluo said: "I was misled by Huai'en and have deeply failed the Duke; now I ask to exert my utmost for the Duke and strike the Tibetans to atone for my fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yaogeluo said: "Huai'en misled me, and I have wronged you deeply; let me now do my utmost for you and strike the Tibetans to make amends.

sentences.zh: 然懷恩之子，可敦兄弟也，願捨之勿殺。」

translations.literal: Yet Huai'en's son is the qaghan's brother-in-law; I wish him spared — do not kill him."
translations.idiomatic: But Huai'en's son is the qaghan's brother-in-law; I ask that you spare him."

sentences.zh: 子儀許之。

translations.literal: Ziyi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi consented.

sentences.zh: 回紇觀者左右為兩翼，稍前，子儀麾下亦進，子儀揮手卻之，因取酒與其酋長共飲。

translations.literal: Uyghur onlookers formed wings left and right and advanced slightly; Ziyi's followers also moved forward; Ziyi waved them back, then took wine and drank with their chieftains together.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur spectators closed in on both flanks; Ziyi's men started forward too, but Ziyi waved them back, then shared wine with the chieftains.

sentences.zh: 藥葛羅使子儀先執酒為誓，子儀酹地曰：「大唐天子萬歲！

translations.literal: Yaogeluo had Ziyi first take wine and swear; Ziyi poured libation on the ground, saying: "Long live the Son of Heaven of Great Tang!
translations.idiomatic: Yaogeluo had Ziyi drink first and swear; Ziyi poured a libation and said: "Long live the Son of Heaven of Great Tang!

sentences.zh: 回紇可汗亦萬歲！

translations.literal: Long live the Uyghur Qaghan also!
translations.idiomatic: Long live the Uyghur qaghan!

sentences.zh: 兩國將相亦萬歲！

translations.literal: Long live the generals and ministers of both countries also!
translations.idiomatic: Long live the generals and ministers of both realms!

sentences.zh: 有負約者，身殞陳前，家族滅絕。」

translations.literal: Whoever breaks the covenant — let his person perish before the battle line and his clan be exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever breaks this oath — let him die on the field and his clan be wiped out."

sentences.zh: 杯至藥葛羅，亦酹地曰：「如令公誓！」

translations.literal: When the cup reached Yaogeluo, he too poured libation on the ground and said: "As the Duke swears!"
translations.idiomatic: When the cup came to Yaogeluo, he too poured a libation and said: "As the Duke swears!"

sentences.zh: 於是諸酋長皆大喜曰：「向以二巫師從軍，巫言此行甚安穩，不與唐戰，見一大人而還，今果然矣。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the chieftains all rejoiced greatly, saying: "Formerly two shamans accompanied the army; the shamans said this expedition would be very safe, that we would not fight Tang and would see a great man and return — now it is exactly so."
translations.idiomatic: Then the chiefs rejoiced and said: "We brought two shamans with us; they said this march would be safe, that we would not fight Tang but would see a great man and return — and so it has proved."

sentences.zh: 子儀遺之彩三千匹，酋長分以賞巫。

translations.literal: Ziyi gave them three thousand bolts of colored silk; the chieftains divided it to reward the shamans.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi gave them three thousand bolts of colored silk; the chiefs divided it among the shamans as reward.

sentences.zh: 子儀竟與定約而還。

translations.literal: Ziyi finally settled the covenant with them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sealed the pact and returned.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃聞之，夜，引兵遁去。

translations.literal: The Tibetans heard of it; by night they led troops and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans heard, they withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 回紇遣其酋長石野那等六人入見天子。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs sent their chieftains Shiyena and five others to enter and see the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs sent six chieftains, including Shiyena, to audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 藥葛羅帥眾追吐蕃，子儀使白元光帥精騎與之俱；

translations.literal: Yaogeluo led his host in pursuit of the Tibetans; Ziyi sent Bai Yuanguang to lead crack cavalry to go with them;
translations.idiomatic: Yaogeluo pursued the Tibetans, and Ziyi sent Bai Yuanguang with elite cavalry to join him;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，戰於靈台西原，大破之，殺吐蕃萬計，得所掠士女四千人。

translations.literal: On guiyou they fought on the west plain of Lingtai, routing them completely; Tibetan dead were counted by the ten thousands; they recovered four thousand men and women who had been plundered.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou they fought on the west plain of Lingtai and routed the enemy; Tibetan dead ran into the tens of thousands, and four thousand captives were recovered.

sentences.zh: 丙子，又破之於涇州東。

translations.literal: On bingzi they again routed them east of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi they defeated them again east of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，僕固懷恩將張休藏等降。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Pugu Huai'en's generals Zhang Xiucang and others surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Zhang Xiucang and other generals of Pugu Huai'en surrendered.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔罷親征，京城解嚴。

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict was issued discontinuing the personal campaign; the capital was stood down from alert.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi an edict ended the emperor's personal campaign and the capital stood down from alert.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗以陝西節度使郭英乂領神策軍，使內侍魚朝恩監其軍；

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Suzong had the Shaanxi military commissioner Guo Yingyi command the Shence Army, with the palace eunuch Yu Chaoen to supervise that army;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Suzong had placed the Shaanxi commissioner Guo Yingyi in command of the Shence Army, with the palace eunuch Yu Chaoen as army supervisor;

sentences.zh: 英乂入為僕射，朝恩專將之。

translations.literal: Yingyi entered court as Vice Director of the Left Department; Chaoen alone commanded it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingyi entered court as vice director, Chaoen took sole command.

sentences.zh: 及上幸陝，朝恩舉在陝兵與神策軍迎扈，悉號神策軍，天子幸其營。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Shaan, Chaoen mustered the troops then in Shaan together with the Shence Army to escort and guard him; all were styled the Shence Army; the Son of Heaven favored their camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Shaan, Chaoen combined the troops there with the Shence Army to escort him; all were called Shence troops, and the emperor lodged in their camp.

sentences.zh: 及京師平，朝恩遂以軍歸禁中，自將之，然尚未得與北軍齒。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, Chaoen thereupon brought the army back to the inner palace and commanded it himself, but had not yet attained parity with the Northern Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was recovered, Chaoen brought the army into the inner palace and kept personal command, though it had not yet won equal standing with the Northern Army.

sentences.zh: 至是，朝恩以神策軍從上屯苑中，其勢浸盛，分為左、右廂，居北軍之右矣。

translations.literal: At this time Chaoen followed the emperor in encamping in the palace park with the Shence Army; its power gradually grew great; it was divided into left and right wings and occupied a position to the right of the Northern Army.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chaoen followed the emperor into camp in the palace grounds with the Shence Army; its power swelled, it was split into left and right wings, and it took its place to the right of the Northern Army.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀以僕固名臣、李建忠等皆懷恩驍將，恐逃入外夷，請招之。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, because Pugu Mingchen, Li Jianzhong, and others were all Huai'en's crack generals, feared they would flee into foreign lands and requested that they be summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, knowing that Pugu Mingchen, Li Jianzhong, and others had been Huai'en's fiercest generals, feared they might flee to the barbarians and asked that they be offered surrender.

sentences.zh: 名臣，懷恩之侄也，時在回紇營。

translations.literal: Mingchen, Huai'en's nephew, was then in the Uyghur camp.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen, Huai'en's nephew, was at that time in the Uyghur camp.

sentences.zh: 上敕並舊將有功者皆赦其罪，令回紇送之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that former generals who had rendered merit should all have their crimes pardoned and directed the Uyghurs to send them in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned the crimes of all former generals who had served with merit and ordered the Uyghurs to send them to court.

sentences.zh: 壬午，名臣以千餘騎來降。

translations.literal: On renwu Mingchen came to surrender with more than a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Mingchen surrendered with more than a thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子儀使開府儀同三司慕容休貞以書諭党項帥鄭庭、郝德等，皆詣鳳翔降。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent Kaifu Yitong Sansi Murong Xiuzhen with letters to persuade the Tangut chiefs Zheng Ting, Hao De, and others; all came to Fengxiang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent Murong Xiuzhen, honorary Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with letters urging the Tangut chiefs Zheng Ting, Hao De, and others to submit; they all came to Fengxiang and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 甲申，周智光詣闕獻捷，再宿歸鎮。

translations.literal: On jiashen Zhou Zhiguang came to court to present his victory report; after two nights' lodging he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Zhou Zhiguang came to court to report his victory; he stayed two nights and then returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 智光負專殺之罪未治，上既遣而悔之。

translations.literal: Zhiguang bore the crime of unauthorized killing, which had not yet been punished; the emperor, having let him go, regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang had committed unauthorized killings that had gone unpunished; after letting him depart, the emperor regretted his leniency.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，回紇胡祿都督等二百餘人入見，前後贈賚繒帛十萬匹；

translations.literal: On yiyou more than two hundred Uyghur Heluhulu Tutuq and others were received in audience; in all, before and after, one hundred thousand bolts of silk were bestowed as gifts;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou more than two hundred Uyghur chiefs including the Heluhulu Tutuq were received in audience; in all, one hundred thousand bolts of silk were lavished on them as gifts;

sentences.zh: 府藏空竭，稅百官俸以給之。

translations.literal: the treasury was emptied and officials' salaries were levied to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: the treasury was exhausted, and officials' salaries were taxed to pay for it.
